5.9 Unpaid Leave (Non-FMLA)

Available accrued time off (to include personal leave and vacation leave) must be
exhausted prior to the use of unpaid personal leave. The Village Administrator, or
designee, may approve unpaid personal leave in amount subject to the discretion of
the Village Administrator.


5.10 Jury Duty

A full-time employee, while serving upon a jury in any court of record, shall be paid
their regular salary for each of their workdays during the time so served. Jury duty
fees paid to the employee by the court shall be returned to the Village. The
employee, upon notice of jury service, shall present such notice to their supervisor.
A copy of such notice shall be filed in the employee's personnel file. Jury service
requiring less than four (4) hours of the employee's regular work day as verified by
the time report, shall require the employee to report to their supervisor for
completion of their regular work day with the Village.


5.11 Lactation Breaks

Employees who have recently given birth will be allowed a reasonable break time in
order to nurse or express breast milk, for up to one year after the child’s birth. The
employee will be provided appropriate space, other than a bathroom, that is shielded
from view and free from intrusion from employees and members of the public.
Lactation breaks under this policy should, to the extent possible, run concurrently
with any other break time available to the employee.


5.12 Travel Reimbursement

Village employees may be reimbursed for allowable expenses incurred while
traveling out-of-village on official Village business. All travel must be approved in
advance. Receipts are required. Overnight travel must be approved by the
Department Head and the Village Director of Finance. All reimbursements are
subject to the regulations contained herein and compliance with established
procedures:

       5.12.1 Reimbursable Expenses:

          •   Commercial air flights - reimbursement is available for air flight
              expenses only when the cost of such flight is less than the cost of
              automobile mileage, or where travel time is of significance.



                                      32


                                                                       Village of Plain City
                                              Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                               Revised ___________, 2026
          •   Bus or taxi - employees are to use the most economical means
              available when traveling on Village business via bus or taxi.
          •   Automobile - whenever possible, Village vehicles will be utilized for
              travel to and from meetings and conventions. If no vehicle is available
              and an employee is required to use his/her privately owned vehicle, he
              or she shall be provided mileage reimbursement at the IRS
              reimbursement rate. Such payment is considered to be total
              reimbursement for all vehicle-related expenses (e.g., gas, oil,
              depreciation, insurance, etc.). Mileage reimbursement is payable to
              only one of two or more employees traveling on the same trip, in the
              same vehicle. Rental of a vehicle is not reimbursable without prior
              approval.
          •   Meals - Expenses incurred for meals while on official business will be
              reimbursed at actual cost with the approval of the Department Head.
              Approval must be granted prior to the employee incurring the expense.
              An employee is eligible for such reimbursement only when travel has
              been authorized, in writing, and when travel extends through a normal
              meal period. If meal expenses are included in registration fees,
              duplicate meals shall not be reimbursable.
          •   Lodging - employees will be reimbursed for reasonable and necessary
              lodging expenses at the single room rate.
          •   Phone Calls - phone calls necessary for official Village business are
              reimbursable.
          •   Parking and Tolls - expenses for parking, highway, bridge and tunnel
              tolls are reimbursable. Parking expenses include parking within and
              outside the Village.
          •   Emergency road service, towing, and repair charges – incurred while
              operating Village-owned vehicles on official Village business.

      5.12.2 Non-Reimbursable Expenses:

          •   Alcoholic beverages;
          •   Entertainment;
          •   Laundry and dry cleaning;
          •   Room service charges;
          •   Expenses of spouse traveling with employee; and
          •   Any otherwise allowable expense where no receipt is provided by the
              employee. Expense reports shall be timely filed by employees detailing
              all costs with receipts attached.

The use of a Village-owned vehicle is a privilege. Employees operating a Village
motor vehicle are required to have a proper and valid motor vehicle operator’s
license.

Any Village employee, who operates a Village-owned motor vehicle or a privately
owned motor vehicle in the discharge of official Village business, shall at all times
during the course of operation, fully utilize the front seat occupant restraint systems
provided in the vehicles and require like use of said systems by any passengers in the
vehicle.

Employees who operate Village vehicles must have appropriate personal insurance
coverage. The Village maintains insurance coverage on Village-owned vehicles
covering bodily injury and property damage resulting from vehicle accidents.

Use of a Village-owned vehicle must be pre-approved by the employee’s supervisor.
Employees shall not use, or permit the use of Village vehicles for any purpose other
than official Village business. Passengers not on official Village business (i.e.,
children, spouses, friends, hitchhikers, etc.) are not permitted in Village-owned
vehicles. Employees, as representatives of the Village, are expected to be courteous
to the public and to obey all traffic laws. Village employees should drive and conduct
themselves so as to enhance the reputation of the Village.

Employees who drive Village vehicles or who drive their personal vehicles for Village
business are subject to periodic (at least annual) record checks at the Bureau of
Motor Vehicles. Employees who utilize Village vehicles are responsible for reporting
to their supervisor any moving traffic violations obtained while on, or off, duty as an
employee’s personal driving record may impact his/her ability to be covered on the
Village’s liability policy. Employees who drive on behalf of the Village are subject to
reassignment and/or discipline in the event of a license revocation, suspension or
traffic offense conviction.

Concerns regarding repairs or maintenance to Village vehicles must be reported to
the employee’s immediate supervisor.


5.14 Tools, Supplies and Equipment

Employees shall not use or permit the use of Village-owned tools, supplies and/or
equipment for any purposes other than official Village business. Personal use of
Village-owned tools, supplies and/or equipment is strictly prohibited.

an amount equal to 50% of the Village’s annual premium cost for single coverage.

The employee shall provide adequate proof of insurance of private medial health
care coverage. This opt-out program does not extend to dental and vision
insurance.


5.17 Tuition Reimbursement

The continuing education and development of all employees is most desirable; in
order to encourage such advancement an Educational Assistance Program is
offered. The Village will pay up to 80% of the tuition, necessary fees, and course
materials for courses related to the development of a regular full-time employee
that would otherwise be paid by the employee subject to annual appropriation by
Council. The Village Administrator may apply this concept to cover fees and costs
of training and higher education programs which he/she determines to qualify as an
appropriate employee benefit. This Program does not pertain to customary and
standard training and certification costs required by law or administrative policy of
the Village that are required or necessary for employees to perform their specific
job functions and have been typically paid for by the Village in the past.

To be eligible to participate in this Program, the employee must complete a
Request for Educational Assistance form for each course and the form must be
approved by the employee's Department Head and the Village Administrator.
Employees should submit one copy of the form and receive approval prior to
starting any course. Upon satisfactorily completing the course, the employee must
provide the Village with proof of satisfactory completion, as well as a copy of proof
of tuition and necessary fee and textbook payments from the educational
institution, in order to receive reimbursement.

At his/her option, an employee eligible to participate in the Village’s Educational
Assistance Program by having completed and received approval on a Request for

      6.1 Code of Ethics

      All Village employees are expected to maintain the highest possible ethical and moral
      standards, and to perform their duties within the laws of the State of Ohio and other
      rules and regulations set forth by the Department Head. Conduct that interferes with
      normal office operations, brings discredit to the Village, is illegal, or is offensive to
      the public or fellow employees, will not be tolerated. Such conduct includes, but is
      not limited to:

         •   engagement in any business or any other interest which is in conflict with the
             proper discharge of official Village duties;
         •   disclosure of confidential information, without proper authorization,
             regarding the property, government or affairs of the Village;

                                             36


                                                                         Village of Plain City
                                                Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                                 Revised ___________, 2026
   •   use of confidential information or influence of official Village position to
       advance personal, financial or other private interests;
   •   acceptance of any gift, in the form of service, loan, item or promise from any
       person, firm or organization which maintains an interest in any business
       dealings with the Village;
   •   acceptance of any gift, in the form of service, loan, item or promise from any

       the proper discharge of official Village duties;
   •   engaging in any matter which is a conflict of interest with the Village or
       undermines the integrity of Village government and/or administration.


6.2 Unlawful Discrimination and Harassment

The Village is committed to providing a facility that is safe and free from unlawful
discrimination and harassment. Unlawful discrimination or harassment is behavior
directed toward an employee because of his/her membership in a protected class
such as: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, ancestry, disability, genetic
information, or military status. Unlawful discrimination and harassment is
inappropriate and illegal and will not be tolerated. All forms of unlawful
discrimination and harassment are governed by this policy and must be reported and
addressed in accordance with this policy.


       6.2.1 Definitions

       Unlawful discrimination occurs when individuals are treated less favorably in
       their employment because of their membership in a protected classification.
       An employer may not discriminate against an individual with respect to the
       terms and conditions of

       employment, such as promotions, raises, and other job opportunities, based
       upon that individual’s membership in that protected class.

       Harassment is a form of discrimination. Harassment is unwelcome conduct
       that is based upon a protected classification. Harassment becomes unlawful
       where: (1) enduring the offensive conduct becomes a condition of continued
       employment; and/or, (2) the conduct is severe or pervasive enough to create
       a work environment that a reasonable person would consider intimidating,
       hostile, or abusive.

       Sexual harassment is one type of unlawful harassment. Unwelcome sexual
       advances, requests for sexual favors, and other verbal or physical conduct of
       a sexual nature constitute sexual harassment when: (1) submission to the
       conduct is made either explicitly or implicitly a term or condition of an

                                       37


                                                                  Village of Plain City
                                         Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                          Revised ___________, 2026
individual's employment; (2) submission to or rejection of such conduct by an
individual is used as the basis for employment decisions affecting such
individual; or, (3) such conduct has the purpose or effect of unreasonably
interfering with an individual's work performance or creating an intimidating,
hostile, or offensive work environment. Harassment on the basis of an
employee’s membership in any protected classification is unlawful, will not be
tolerated, and must be reported.

6.2.2 Examples

Unlawful discrimination and harassment do not generally encompass
conduct of a socially acceptable nature. However, some conduct that is
appropriate in a social setting may be inappropriate in the work place. A
victim’s perceived acquiescence in the behavior does not negate the
existence of unlawful discrimination or harassment. Inappropriate conduct
that an employee perceives as being “welcome” by another employee may
form the basis of a legitimate complaint.

6.2.3 Complaint Procedure

Employees who feel they have been subject to unlawful discrimination or
harassment by a fellow employee, supervisor, or other individual affiliated
with the Village shall expediently report the conduct, in writing, to their
supervisor, Department Head or Village Administrator. If the employee is a
direct report of the Village Administrator, they may submit, in writing, a report
of conduct to the Director of Law, who will immediately forward the complaint
to Village Council for consideration. Similarly, employees who feel they have
witnessed discrimination or harassment, or who have questions or concerns
regarding discrimination or harassment, shall immediately contact their
supervisor or Department Head or Village Administrator. Late reporting of
complaints will not, in and of itself, preclude the Village from taking remedial
action. However, so that a thorough and accurate investigation may be
conducted, employees are encouraged to submit complaints in writing and in
an expedient manner following the harassing or offensive incident. All
supervisors are required to follow up on all claims or concerns, whether
written or verbal, regarding unlawful discrimination and harassment.

Although employees may confront the alleged harasser at their discretion,
they are also required to submit a written report of any alleged incidents of
harassment or discrimination through their supervisor or Department Head
or Village Administrator. If the employee is a direct report of the Village
Administrator, they may submit, in writing, a report of conduct to the Director
of Law, who will immediately forward the complaint to Village Council for
consideration. When the Village is notified of the alleged harassment, it will

                                38


                                                                  Village of Plain City
                                         Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                          Revised ___________, 2026
timely investigate the complaint. The investigation may include private
interviews of the employee allegedly harassed, the employee committing the
alleged harassment, and any witnesses. To the extent required by applicable
law, information will be kept as confidential as practicable. All employees are
required to cooperate in any investigation of a harassment complaint.
Determinations of harassment shall be made on a case-by-case basis. If the
investigation reveals the complaint is valid, prompt attention and disciplinary
action designed to stop the harassment and prevent its recurrence will be
taken.

6.2.4 Retaliation

Anti-discrimination laws prohibit retaliatory conduct against individuals who
file a discrimination charge, testify, or participate in any way in an
investigation, proceeding, or lawsuit under these laws; or who oppose
employment practices that they reasonably believe discriminate against
protected individuals, in violation of these laws. The law also prevents
retaliatory conduct against individuals who are close personal friends or
family members with an individual who engaged in protected conduct.
Supervisors and employees shall not in any way retaliate against an individual
for filing a complaint, reporting harassment, participating in an investigation,
or engaging in any other protected activity. Any employee who feels that he
or she has been subjected to retaliatory conduct as a result of actions taken
under this policy, or as a result of his/her relationship with an individual who
took action under this policy, shall immediately report such conduct to their
supervisor or Department Head, or if neither of those individuals is
appropriate, to the Village Administrator. If the employee is a direct report of
the Village Administrator, they may submit, in writing, a report of conduct to
the Director of Law, who will immediately forward the complaint to Village
Council for consideration. Any person found to have retaliated against an
individual for engaging in activity protected by this policy will be subject to
discipline. Disciplinary action for filing a false complaint is not a retaliatory
act.

6.2.5 False Complaints

Legitimate complaints made in good faith are strongly encouraged; however,
false complaints or complaints made in bad faith will not be tolerated. Failure
to prove unlawful discrimination or harassment will not constitute a false
complaint without further evidence of bad faith. False complaints are
considered to be a violation of this policy and an employee who makes a false
complaint may be subject to discipline.




                                39


                                                                  Village of Plain City
                                         Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                          Revised ___________, 2026
6.2.6 Corrective Action

If the Village determines unlawful discrimination, harassment, or retaliation
has taken place, appropriate corrective action will be taken, up to and
including termination. The corrective action will be designed to stop the
unlawful conduct and prevent its recurrence. If appropriate, law enforcement
agencies or other licensing bodies will be notified. Any individual exhibiting
retaliatory or harassing behavior towards an employee who exercised a right
under this policy, or who is a close personal friend or family member of
someone who exercised a right under this policy, will be subject to discipline,
as will any employee who has knowledge of unlawful conduct and allows that
conduct to go unaddressed.

6.2.7 Off-Duty Conduct

Unlawful discrimination or harassment that affects an individual’s
employment may extend beyond the confines of the workplace. Conduct that
occurs off-duty and off premises may also be subject to this policy.

6.2.8 Workplace Romances

To avoid concerns of sexual harassment and other inappropriate behavior,
employees are required to inform their supervisor or Department Head (or if
neither of those individuals is appropriate, to the Village Administrator) if they
currently are, or if they intend to become, romantically involved with a co-
worker. Such relationships are not necessarily prohibited, but must be
appropriately addressed. Should the Village determine that a conflict exists
between an employee’s employment and a personal relationship with a co-
worker, the Village will attempt to work with the employees to resolve the
conflict. Should operational needs prevent resolution, the relationship must
cease or one or both of the parties must separate from employment.
Supervisors are expressly prohibited from engaging in romantic or sexual
relationships with any employee they directly, or indirectly, supervise.

6.2.9 Coverage

This policy covers all employees, supervisors, Department Heads and elected
officials. Additionally, this policy covers all suppliers, subcontractors,
residents, visitors, clients, volunteers and any other individual who enters
property, conducts business on property or on the Village’s behalf, or who is
served by Village personnel.

6.3 Computer Use Policy

      6.3.1 Village Owned Devices

      Village computers and information systems are Village property. They may be
      used only for explicitly authorized purposes. Village computers, internet,
      email, text messages and other online services shall be used for business
      purposes only. Access to any internet site or service using Village-owned
      equipment, which does not further Village business, is strictly prohibited on-
      duty or off-duty. Improper use of Village computers, internet or email, or
      texting may result in discipline, up to and including termination.

      The Village reserves the right to examine all data stored in or transmitted by
      their computers and systems. Employees shall be aware that computer,
      internet and email usage can and will be monitored by the Village, without
      notice. These actions may be taken for business-purpose inquiries including
      but not limited to theft investigation, unauthorized disclosure of confidential
      business or proprietary information, excessive personal use of the system, or
      monitoring work flow and employee productivity. Employees shall have no
      expectation of privacy in Village computers or information accessed or
      disseminated on Village computers.

      Employees shall be aware that their personal and professional on-duty and
      off-duty use of Village computers, internet, email and texting can and will be
      monitored by the Village. Employees shall have no expectation of privacy in
      Village computers or information accessed or disseminated on those
      computers or on Village information systems. Employee use of Village
      computers constitutes the employee’s consent to the Village reviewing the
      employee’s computer history and use, including password-protected
      websites/email and deleted material, so that the Village may ensure
      compliance with this policy.

      6.3.2 Personally Owned Devices

      The Village may reimburse employees for part of the expenses or all of the
      expenses incurred by the employees in using their personally owned
      electronic devices for Village business.

      Regardless of whether the Village reimburses an employee for his/her
      electronic device, access to the internet, email or other online services using
      personally-owned electronic devices (i.e. cell phones, iPad) for personal
      matters while on-duty is also strictly prohibited. Paid work time is to be
      dedicated to work-related activities. Employees who access the internet and
      or engage in work-related communications or communications which may

                                     41

                                               Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook

       affect workplace operations while on-duty using a personally-owned
       electronic device shall have no expectation of privacy in that access or
       communication.

       Relatedly, employees shall have no expectation of privacy in personally-
       owned electronic devices (i.e. cell phones, iPad) which are used off-duty and
       involve work-related communications or communications which may affect
       workplace operations.


6.4 Social Media

The Village supports the free exchange of information and camaraderie among
employees on the internet. However, when internet blogging, chat room
discussions, email, text messages or other forms of electronic communication
extend to employees revealing confidential information about the Village or its
employees, or engaging in posting inappropriate material about the Village or its
employees, the employee who posts such information or assists in posting such
material may be subject to disciplinary action.

Employees are reminded to be careful of the information they disclose on the
internet, including social media sites. The following uses of social media are strictly
prohibited, whether on or off duty:

   1) Comments or displays about coworkers, supervisors or the Village that are
      vulgar, obscene, threatening, intimidating, harassing, or a violation of the
      Village’s workplace policies against discrimination, harassment or retaliation.
   2) Statements or uses of the Village’s logo which are slanderous or detrimental,
      including evidence of the misuse of the Village’s authority, information,
      insignia or equipment.
   3) Unprofessional communication which, if left unaddressed, could potentially
      result in a civil or criminal cause of action against the Village. Unprofessional
      communication also includes that which the Village could demonstrate has a
      substantial risk of negatively affecting the Village’s reputation, mission or
      operations, such as slander, defamation or other legal cause of action.
   4) Disclosure of confidential and/or proprietary information acquired in the
      course of employment.            Confidential information includes not only
      information that would not be available pursuant to a public records request,
      but also includes any information which does not relate to an issue of public
      concern.
   5) Comments or displays which impact employees’ abilities to perform their job
      duties or the Village’s ability to maintain an efficient workplace.

Social media sites may be inspected by the Village for cause to determine potential
policy violations. If an employee believes that an online communication violates a

Village policy, the employee should immediately report the communication to
his/her supervisor. The Village may investigate the matter, determine whether such

This policy does not apply to communications protected by the U.S. or Ohio

collective bargaining or other mutual aid and protection.


6.5 Discipline

The Village generally follows the principles of progressive discipline wherein it
provides employees with notice of deficiencies and an opportunity to improve.
However, most Village employees are “at-will”, serving at the pleasure of the Village.
At-will employees may resign or be terminated at any time for any reason to the
extent permitted by applicable law. Nothing contained in this Handbook shall be
construed to modify the status of Village employees as “at-will” employees. Further,
nothing contained in this Handbook shall be construed, in any way, to restrict the
Village’s right to bypass one or all of the progressive discipline procedures set forth
below.
Potential disciplinary action includes:

   1) Oral reprimands (with appropriate notation in employee’s file)
   2) Written reprimands
   3) Suspension with or without pay
   4) Demotion
   5) Termination
   6) Other discipline as may be appropriate

The Village will endeavor to give employees an understanding as to the requirements
of their position and of public employment. Instructions may be verbal or written.
Employees are expected to obey all lawful verbal and written orders and directives
from all supervisory staff. If an employee feels that an order is unreasonable, he or
she should obey the order under protest then bring the matter to the attention of the
next-level supervisor.

The property, image, and reputation of the Village is to be respected at all times. Due
to the public nature of employment with the Village, an employee’s off-duty conduct
that affects the Village may form the basis for discipline. Any comments or
questions concerning the standard of conduct expected should be directed toward
the employee’s immediate supervisor.

Certain Village employees, such as police officers, may only be terminated for
reasons set forth by law or collective bargaining agreement and/or may have other


                                      43


                                                                        Village of Plain City
                                               Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                                Revised ___________, 2026
rights such as an appeal to Village Council. Employees who work for the Police
Department should consult the Operations Manual for disciplinary procedures.

       6.5.1 Personnel Board of Appeals

       In all cases of discipline, excluding probationary appeals, resulting in
       suspension (4 or more days without pay), demotion or discharge, the
       Appointing Authority shall furnish such employee with a copy of the order of
       suspension, demotion, or dismissal together with the reasons for same if
       the employee chooses to appeal the action. Upon appeal, the employee
       must file a written explanation explaining the situation and why they are
       choosing to appeal; copies thereof shall be filed with the Administrator and
       the Clerk (or designee) of the Personnel Board of Appeals. The written
       explanation supplied therein with the Administrator and the Personnel Board
       of Appeals shall be for informational purposes only and shall be made within
       five (5) BUSINESS days from the employee's receipt of notice of discipline.
       The effective date of any such disciplinary action shall not be affected by the
       filing date of such written explanation.
       The Personnel Board of Appeals shall promptly set a date and time for a
       hearing on such an appeal, and at such hearing the appellant may appear in
       person or by counsel, and the Administrator and/or Department/Division
       head may likewise appear in person or by counsel, and each may offer such
       evidence upon the matter as may be pertinent and relevant. Upon
       conclusion of the hearing, the Personnel Board of Appeals may affirm or
       disaffirm the judgment of the Appointing Authority as to any disciplinary
       action involving suspension without pay for four (4) or more days, or
       demotion, or dismissal. The decision of the Personnel Board of Appeals
       shall be final subject only to court action.


6.6 Appearance

Each Department Head reserves the right to set appropriate dress and grooming
standards for all employees in order to present and project a professional image. The
standard uniform or dress code approved by the Department Head will be worn and
adhered to by all employees. An employee's clothing and overall appearance must be
appropriate, in good taste, and present a favorable public image as a representative
of the Village. Clothing shall at all times be conducive to the safe and effective
performance of required job duties.

VII.      HEALTH AND SAFETY

       7.1 Workplace Accidents

       An employee who is injured and/or involved in an accident arising out of and in the
       course of employment must notify his/her supervisor immediately and must
       complete an accident report recording all pertinent and factual information about
       the accident. This report must be completed for each work-related accident or
       injury, whether or not the employee requires medical attention. The report is to be
       forwarded to the Department Head within twenty-four (24) hours of the accident
       and/or injury. In the event of a serious injury, the Department Head must be notified
       immediately so that an investigation can be initiated. Employees involved in any
       workplace accident may be subject to immediate mandatory drug/alcohol testing.


       7.2 Workplace Violence

       The Village is committed to providing a work environment that is safe, secure and
       free of harassment, threats, intimidation and violence. In furtherance of this
       commitment, the Village enforces a zero-tolerance policy for workplace violence.
       Consistent with this policy, threats or acts of physical violence, including
       intimidation, harassment, and/or coercion which involve or affect employees, or
       which occur on Village property or at a worksite, will not be tolerated. Employees
       who are found to have committed acts of workplace violence will receive discipline
       and possible criminal prosecution, depending on the nature of the offense.

       Prohibited acts of workplace violence include, but are not limited to, the following:

          1) hitting or shoving;
          2) threatening harm to an employee or his/her family, friends, associates, or
             property;
          3) intentional destruction of property;
          4) harassing or threatening telephone calls, letters or other forms of written or
             electronic communications, including email and website postings;
          5) intimidating or attempting to coerce an employee to do wrongful acts, as
             defined by applicable law, administrative rule, policy, or work rule;
          6) willful, malicious and repeated following of another person, also known as
             “stalking” and/or making threats with the intent to place another person in
             reasonable fear for his/her safety;
          7) suggesting or otherwise intimating that an act to injure persons or property
             is “appropriate”, without regard to the location where the suggestion or
             intimation occurs; and
          8) unauthorized possession or inappropriate use of firearms, weapons, or any
             other dangerous devices on Village property.

7.3 Drug and Alcohol Testing

In order to further the Village’s objective of maintaining a safe, healthy, and drug-free
workplace, the Village may require an employee to submit to a drug or alcohol test if
there is reasonable suspicion to believe that an employee is under the influence of a
controlled substance or alcohol, or randomly if the employee occupies a safety-
sensitive position as determined by the employee’s supervisor and Village officials.
Refusal to submit to a drug or alcohol test or a positive test may result in disciplinary
action, up to and including termination.

In 2016, medical marijuana was legalized by the State of Ohio under House Bill 523.
With the passing of this legislation, the Ohio Medical Marijuana Control Program was
established requiring the program be fully operational by September, 2018. As this
time is upon us, it is important that all employees, regardless of capacity, understand
the Village’s position concerning medical marijuana. Marijuana remains a schedule I
controlled substance, regardless of being authorized for medicinal use under Ohio
law. While permissible under state law, medicinal use of marijuana has not been
approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for clinical use. As such,
the use of marijuana, in any form for any purpose, authorized for medicinal purposes
or unauthorized, is prohibited under the Village’s Drug Free Workplace Policy.
Nothing under House Bill 523 requires an employer to permit or accommodate an
employee’s use, possession, or distribution of medical marijuana. In addition, the law
does not prohibit an employer from taking any adverse employment action because
of an employee or prospective employee’s use, possession or distribution or medical
marijuana. Further, the law does not permit a person to sue an employer for taking
an adverse employment action (refusal to hire, discharge or discipline) because of an
employee’s use, possession or distribution of medical marijuana. All employees,
regardless of status, remain subject to testing under the Village’s Drug Free
Workplace policy at any time during their employment, which may include post-
accident, reasonable suspicion and random testing. An employee who is terminated
as a result of medical marijuana use will be considered having been discharged for
just cause under Unemployment Compensation Law and not eligible for benefits.
Additionally, as it pertains to Workers’ Compensation Law, an employee would be
ineligible for compensation and benefits if they were under the influence of
marijuana and being under the influence of marijuana was the proximate cause of
the injury. This applies regardless of whether the marijuana use is recommended by
a physician.

On July 30, 2019, Governor Mike DeWine signed Senate Bill 57 into law, which allows
for the immediate sale of cannabidiol (“CBD”) and hemp cultivation. CBD is one of the
hundreds of chemical components in the marijuana plant. The bill legalizes CBD
products that contain 0.3% THC (Tetrahydrocannabinols) or less. While permissible
under Ohio law, much of the CBD market is unregulated, resulting in some products
containing over the legally permissible amount. While the use of CBD in and of itself,
does not violate village policy, the amount and frequency of CBD use can result in a

                                       46


                                                                         Village of Plain City
                                                Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                                 Revised ___________, 2026
positive drug screening for THC which would be a violation of the Village’s Drug Free
Workplace Policy and would result in discipline. As such, employees are advised that
they use CBD at their own risk.

Where the Village has a reasonable suspicion to believe that an employee is in
violation of this policy, it may require the employee to go a medical clinic, at the
Village’s expense, to provide blood and/or urine specimens. Reasonable suspicion
shall generally mean suspicion based on personal observation by a Village
representative, including descriptions of appearance, behavior, speech, breath, or
inexplicable behavior demonstrating that the employee is under the influence of
and/or dependent on a controlled substance or alcohol.

Any employee who tests positive for controlled substances and/or alcohol while on
duty may request re-testing of the original specimen at their own expense.

Employees subject to random drug testing who refuse to participate in either testing
or any rehabilitation programs offered, or who continued to test positive for said
substances will be terminated.

Employees who are required to hold a commercial driver’s license (CDL) will be
required to participate in the Village’s drug and alcohol testing program as required
by federal law which includes pre-employment testing, post-accident testing,
random testing, reasonable suspicion testing, and return-to-work testing. Policies
and procedures for these programs will be consistent with federal law and will be
made available to employees required to hold CDL’s and their supervisors.

To the extent governed by applicable law, an employee who is found to be under the
influence of drugs or alcohol while on duty may forfeit his/her right to worker’s
compensation benefits and may be required to undergo drug and alcohol testing in
accordance with this policy.

7.4 Vehicle and Building Security

       vehicles should remain in good condition and safety alerts must be reported

       Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is strictly prohibited and

7.5 Exposure Control Plan

The Village of Plain City is committed to providing a safe and healthy work
environment for all employees. In pursuit of this endeavor, the following Exposure
Control Plan (ECP) is provided to eliminate or minimize occupational exposure to
bloodborne pathogens in accordance with OSHA standard 29 CFR 1910.1030,
"Bloodborne Pathogens” (as adopted by the Public Employment Risk Reduction Act).

      7.5.1 Program Administration

      The Village Administrator is responsible for the implementation of the ECP.
      The Public Works Manager will maintain, review, and update the ECP at least
      annually, and whenever necessary to include new or modified tasks and
      procedures.

      Those employees who are determined to have occupational exposure to
      blood or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM) must comply with the
      procedures and work practices outlined in this ECP.

      The Public Works Manager and Pool Manager will maintain and provide all
      necessary personal protective equipment (PPE), engineering controls (e.g.,
      sharps containers), labels, and red bags as required by the standard. The
      Public Works Manager and Pool Manager will ensure that adequate supplies of
      the aforementioned equipment are available in the appropriate sizes.

      The Public Works Manager and Pool Manager will be responsible for ensuring
      that all medical actions required are performed and that appropriate
      employee health and OSHA records are maintained.


                                     48


                                                                  Village of Plain City
                                         Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                          Revised ___________, 2026
The Public Works Manager and Pool Manager will be responsible for training,
documentation of training, and making the written ECP available to
employees, OSHA, and NIOSH representatives.

7.5.2 Employee Exposure Determination

The following is a list of all job classifications within the Village in which all
employees have occupational exposure:

JOB TITLE                                   DEPARTMENT/LOCATION
Maintenance                                 Street Garage
Mechanic                                    Street Garage
Facilities Technician                       Street Garage/Administration
Pool Manager                                Aquatic Center
Pool Employees                              Aquatic Center

7.5.3 Methods of Implementation and Control

   •   Universal Precautions: All employees will utilize Universal
       Precautions. Universal Precautions is an approach to infection
       control. According to the concept of Universal Precautions, all human
       blood and certain human body fluids are treated as if known to be
       infectious for HIV, HBV, and other bloodborne pathogens.
   •   Exposure Control Plan: Employees covered by the bloodborne
       pathogen’s standard receive an explanation of this ECP during their
       initial t-training session. It will also be reviewed in their annual
       refresher training. AD employees have an opportunity to review this
       plan at any time during their work shifts by contacting the Public
       Works Manager and Pool Manager. If requested, the Village will provide
       an employee with a copy of the ECP free of charge and within 15 days
       of the request.

       The Village Administrator is responsible for reviewing and updating
       the ECP annually or more frequently if necessary to reflect any new or
       modified tasks and procedures which affect occupational exposure
       and to reflect new or revised employee positions with occupational
       exposure.

7.5.4 Engineering Controls and Work Practices

Engineering controls and work practice controls will be used to prevent or
minimize exposure to bloodborne pathogens. The specific engineering
controls and work practice controls used are listed below:

   •   glass tubes, slides, stirrers & collection bottles in the laboratory
   •   counter tops

7.5.5 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

PPE is provided to Village employees at no cost to them. Training is provided
by the Public Works Manager and Pool Manager in the use of the appropriate
PPE for the tasks or procedures employees will perform.

The types of PPE available to employees are as follows:

       •   uniforms, gloves, eye protection, etc.

PPE is located at the Public Works Facility, Municipal Building, Aquatic
Center, and may be obtained by employees through their respective
Supervisors.

All employees using PPE must observe the following precautions:

       •   Wash hands immediately or as soon as feasible after removal of
           gloves or other PPE. Remove PPE after it becomes contaminated,
           and before leaving the work area.
       •   Used PPE may be disposed of in appropriate containers for
           storage, laundering, decontamination, or disposal marked as such.
       •   Wear appropriate gloves when it can be reasonably anticipated
           that there may be hand contact with blood or OPIM, and when
           handling or touching contaminated items or surfaces; replace
           gloves if torn, punctured, contaminated, or if their ability to
           function as a barrier is compromised.
       •   Utility gloves may be decontaminated for reuse if their integrity is
           not compromised; discard utility gloves if they show signs of
           cracking, peeling, tearing, puncturing, or deterioration.
       •   Never wash or decontaminate disposable gloves for reuse.




                               50


                                                                 Village of Plain City
                                        Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                         Revised ___________, 2026
       •   Wear appropriate face and eye protection when splashes, sprays,
           spatters, or droplets of blood or OPIM pose a hazard to the eye,
           nose, or mouth.
       •   Remove immediately or as soon as feasible any garment
           contaminated by blood or OPIM, in such a way as to avoid contact
           with the outer surface.

The procedure for handling used PPE is as follows:

       •   Gloves must be utilized in handling of all contaminated materials.
           All tools, equipment etc. shall be placed in protective containers
           until decontamination procedures are followed.
       •   Decontamination shall be completed using protective clothing and
           occur at the Public Works Facility or at a location designated by the
           Public Works Manager in accordance with approved methods.

7.5.6 Housekeeping

Regulated waste is placed in containers which are closable, constructed to
contain all contents and prevent leakage, appropriately labeled or color-
coded (see Labels), and closed prior to removal to prevent spillage or
protrusion of contents during handling.

Bins and pails (e.g., wash or emesis basins) are cleaned and decontaminated
as soon as feasible after visible contamination.

Broken glassware which may be contaminated is picked up using mechanical
means, such as a brush and dust pan.

7.5.7 Laundry

The following contaminated articles will be laundered by the Village:

       •   All uniforms subject to contamination.

Laundering will be performed by Cintas or other designated companies at
regularly scheduled times.

The following laundering requirements must be met:

       •   handle contaminated laundry as little as possible, with minimal
           agitation;

                                                                 Village of Plain City
                                        Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook

       •   place wet contaminated laundry in leak-proof, labeled or color-
           coded containers before transport. Use red bags or bags marked
           with “biohazard” symbol for this purpose; and
       •   wear appropriate PPE when handling and/or sorting contaminated
           laundry.

EQUIPMENT TO BE LABELED                     LABEL TYPE (size, color, etc.)

7.5.9 Hepatitis B Vaccination

The Public Works Manager and Pool Manager will provide training to
employees on hepatitis B vaccinations, addressing the safety, benefits,
efficacy, methods of administration, and availability.

The hepatitis B vaccination series is available at no cost after training and
within 10 days of initial assignment to employees identified in the exposure
determination section of this plan. Vaccination is encouraged unless:

       •   documentation exists that the employee has previously received
           the series,
       •   antibody testing reveals that the employee is immune, or
       •   medical evaluation shows that vaccination is contra-indicated.

However, if an employee chooses to decline vaccination, the employee must
sign a declination form. Employees who decline may request and obtain the
vaccination at a later date at no cost. Documentation of refusal of the
vaccination is kept within employee personnel files.

Vaccination will be provided by Union County Board of Health in Marysville or
other such arrangement as provided.

                                                                  Village of Plain City
                                         Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook

Following hepatitis B vaccinations, the health care professional's Written
Opinion will be limited to whether the employee requires the hepatitis
vaccine, and whether the vaccine was administered.

7.5.10 Post-Exposure Evaluation and Follow-Up

Should an exposure incident occur, employees should contact the Public
Works Manager and Administration.

An immediately available confidential medical evaluation and follow-up will be
conducted by licensed healthcare professionals. Following the initial first aid
(clean the wound, flush eyes or other mucous membrane, etc.), the following
activities will be performed:

       •   Document the routes of exposure and how the exposure occurred.
       •   Identify and document the source individual (unless the employer
           can establish that identification is infeasible or prohibited by state
           or local law).
       •   Obtain consent and make arrangements to have the source
           individual tested as soon as possible to determine HIV, HCV, and
           HBV infectivity; document that the source individual's test results
           were conveyed to the employee's health care provider.
       •   If the source individual is already known to be FHV, HCV and/or HBV
           positive, new testing need not be performed.
       •   Assure that the exposed employee is provided with the source
           individual's test results and with information about applicable
           disclosure laws and regulations concerning the identity and
           infectious status of the source individual (e.g., laws protecting
           confidentiality).
       •   After obtaining consent, collect exposed employee's blood as soon
           as feasible after exposure incident, and test blood for HBV and FHV
           serological status.
       •   If the employee does not give consent for FIIV serological testing
           during collection of blood for baseline testing, preserve the
           baseline blood sample for at least 90 days; if the exposed employee
           elects to have the baseline sample tested during this waiting
           period, perform testing as soon as feasible.

7.5.11 Administration of Post-Exposure Evaluation and Follow-Up

Administration ensures that healthcare professional(s) responsible for
employee's hepatitis B vaccination and post-exposure evaluation and follow-
up are given a copy of OSHA's bloodborne pathogens standard.



                                53


                                                                Village of Plain City
                                       Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                        Revised ___________, 2026
Administration ensures that the healthcare professional evaluating an
employee after an exposure incident receives the following:

       •   a description of the employee's job duties relevant to the exposure
           incident route(s) of exposure;
       •   circumstances of exposure;
       •   if possible, results of the source individual's blood test; and
       •   relevant employee medical records, including vaccination status.

Administration provides the employee with a copy of the evaluating
healthcare professional’s written opinion within 15 days after completion of
the evaluation.

7.5.12 Procedures for Evaluating the Circumstances Surrounding an
Exposure Incident

Public Works Manager and Administration will review the circumstances of all
exposure incidents to determine:

       •   engineering controls in use at the time;
       •   work practices followed;
       •   a description of the device being used;
       •   protective equipment or clothing that was used at the time of the
           exposure incident (gloves, eye shields, etc.);
       •   location of the incident (O.R., E.R., patient room, etc.);
       •   procedure being performed when the incident occurred; and
       •   employee's training.

If it is determined that revisions need to be made, the Village Administrator
will ensure that appropriate changes are made to this ECP. (Changes may
include an evaluation of safer devices, adding employees to the exposure
determination list, etc.)

7.5.13 Employee Training

All employees who have occupational exposure to bloodborne pathogens
receive training conducted by Red Cross or the Ohio Department of Health.

All employees who have occupational exposure to bloodborne pathogens
receive training on the epidemiology, symptoms, and transmission of
bloodborne pathogen diseases. In addition, the training program covers, at a
minimum, the following elements:

       •   a copy and explanation of the standard;

                               54


                                                                 Village of Plain City
                                        Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                         Revised ___________, 2026
       •   an explanation of our ECP and how to obtain a copy;
       •   an explanation of methods to recognize tasks and other activities
           that may involve exposure to blood and OPIM, including what
           constitutes an exposure incident;
       •   an explanation of the use and limitations of engineering controls,
           work practices, and PPE;
       •   an explanation of the types, uses, location, removal, handling,
           decontamination, and disposal of PPE;
       •   an explanation of the basis for PPE selection information on the
           hepatitis B vaccine, including information on its efficacy, safety,
           method of administration, the benefits of being vaccinated, and
           that the vaccine will be offered free of charge;
       •   information on the appropriate actions to take and persons to
           contact in an emergency involving blood or OPIM;
       •   an explanation of the procedure to follow if an exposure incident
           occurs, including the method of reporting the incident and the
           medical follow-up that will be made available;
       •   information on the post-exposure evaluation and follow-up that
           the employer is required to provide for the employee following an
           exposure incident;
       •   an explanation of the signs and labels and/or color coding required
           by the standard and used by the Village; and
       •   an opportunity for interactive questions and answers with the
           person conducting the training session.

Training materials for the Village are available at the Municipal Building.

7.5.14 Training Records

Training records are completed for each employee upon completion of
training. These documents will be kept for at least three years at the Village
Administrator’s Office.

The training records include:

       •   the dates of the training sessions;
       •   the contents or summary of the training sessions;
       •   the names and qualifications of persons conducting the training;
           and
       •   the names and job titles of all persons attending the training
           sessions.




                                55


                                                                           Village of Plain City
                                                  Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                                   Revised ___________, 2026
           Employee training records are provided upon request to the employee or the
           employee's authorized representative within 15 working days. Such requests
           should be addressed to the Village Administrator

           7.5.15 Medical Records

           Medical records are maintained for each employee with occupational
           exposure in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.1020, "Access to Employee
           Exposure and Medical Records."

           The Village Director of Finance is responsible for maintenance of the required
           medical records. These confidential records are kept at 800 Village
           Boulevard, Plain City, Ohio 43064 for at least the duration of employment plus
           30 years.

           Employee medical records are provided upon request of the employee or to
           anyone having written consent of the employee within 15 working days. Such
           request should be sent to the Village Director of Finance, 800 Village
           Boulevard, Plain City, Ohio 43064.

           7.5.16 OSHA Record Keeping

           An exposure incident is evaluated to determine if the case meets OSHA's
           Record Keeping Requirements (29 CFR 1904). This determination and the
           recording activities are completed by the Village Administrator.



VIII.   MISCELLANEOUS

    8.1 Grievance Procedure

    Employees with complaints related to discrimination and/or harassment should
    follow the procedure set forth in the Discrimination/Harassment section of this
    handbook. Employees with complaints related to termination, demotion or
    suspension of four (4) or more days should follow the procedure set forth in the
    Discipline section of this handbook. Employees with any non-
    discrimination/harassment complaints or termination/demotion/suspension
    should refer to the following grievance procedure:

        1) The employee shall first report any grievance to his/her Department Head.
           The decision of the Department Head in the matter shall be given to the
           employee within five (5) working days of the report of the grievance.
        2) If the employee is dissatisfied with the response received and wishes to
           pursue the matter further, the employee must deliver a written request for a

                                         56


                                                                        Village of Plain City
                                               Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                                Revised ___________, 2026
       meeting to the Administrator within five (5) days of the event in question. The
       written request shall state the nature of the grievance, the decision of the
       Department Head in the matter, and the fact that a meeting with the
       Administrator regarding the grievance is desired. The Administrator shall
       meet with the employee within five (5) working days of receipt of the written
       request. The Administrator’s decision in the matter shall be given to the
       employee within five (5) working days of the meeting.

This grievance procedure shall not in any way affect, control, or impact any
disciplinary action against an employee, and shall not be used as a substitute for any
such disciplinary action.


8.2 Resignation/Retirement

Employees who voluntarily resign or retire should notify their immediate supervisor
at least two (2) weeks in advance of the effective date of resignation. This
requirement may be waived at the discretion of the Department Head.

Employees may not unilaterally revoke their resignation once accepted. Employees
must turn in all Village property, including computer passwords, on or before their
last day of employment. Failure to do so may result in legal action by the Village.


8.3 Public Records

The Ohio Public Records Act is incorporated herein. The Village of Plain City and all
employees shall strictly adhere with Ohio’s Public Records Act, Chapter 149 of the
Ohio Revised Code, and all other applicable provisions of law regarding records.
Further, all Village Departments shall keep a copy of the Public Records Policy and
Records Retention Schedule ready and available for reference at any time. If an
employee receives a request to copy or inspect Village records, the employee must
relay that request to his/her Department Head immediately.


8.4 Fraud Reporting

The Ohio Auditor of State’s Office maintains a system for reporting fraud, including
the misuse of public money by any official or office. The system allows all Ohio
citizens, including public employees, the opportunity to make anonymous
complaints through a toll-free number, the Auditor of State’s website, or the United
States mail. Contact information is as follows:

Telephone:    1-866-FRAUD OH (1-866-372-8364)

U.S. Mail:    Ohio Auditor of State’s Office

               Special Investigations Unit
               88 East Broad Street

               Columbus, OH 43215

Web:           www.ohioauditor.gov


8.5 Credit Card Usage
The following Village employees are authorized to hold a credit card:

   1) Director of Finance
   2) Park and Recreation Director
   3) Public Service Supervisor
   4) Administrator
   5) Development Director
   6) Chief of Police

All Village credit card accounts shall be in the name of the “Village of Plain City, Ohio.”
Credit Cards are non-transferable and may not be used by any employee of the
Village except for the Authorized Card Holder.

Credit cards may be utilized only for purchases related to the business and activities
of the Village of Plain City. Village credit card accounts may not be used to purchase
the following items:

   1) Personal items;
   2) Alcohol and entertainment;
   3) Controlled substances requiring a DEA license;
   4) Employee relocation and relocation-related expenses;
   5) Purchases that involve signing an agreement, license, or contract (e.g.,
       leases);
   6) Long term rentals (1 year or longer);
   7) Contracted or personal service providers - specific to unincorporated 1099
       service providers (e.g., photographic studios, dry cleaners, physicians,
       medical labs, auto towing or repair, etc.);
   8) Weapons or ammunition;
   9) Donations;
   10) Fuel for a privately-owned vehicle or aircraft.

Employees using Village-issued cards are responsible for safeguarding the card. If
inappropriate use of the card is discovered, disciplinary action up to and including
discharge from employment is possible. In the event of fraudulent use, the Village
may pursue legal prosecution.


                                        58


                                                                         Village of Plain City
                                                Employee Policies and Procedures Handbook
                                                                 Revised ___________, 2026

Improper costs associated with prohibited purchases will be collected by requesting
the employee voluntarily repay the Village, by the employee voluntarily agreeing to a
payroll deduction or by any legal action available to the Village.

The Director of Finance and the Law Department should be consulted immediately if
credit card misuse is suspected.         The Director of Finance will initiate an
investigation regarding the alleged credit card misuse. During this investigation, the
employee shall be given an opportunity to respond to the allegations being
investigated.

Following the interview with the employee and completion of the investigation, a
final written report will be presented to the Administrator and Director of Law.

Cardholders should not pay Ohio sales tax. The cardholder must tell in-state
suppliers the Village is exempt from Ohio sales tax. A copy of the Village's Tax-
Exempt Certificate is available upon request. If grant funds are being charged,
cardholders are responsible for seeing that all granting agency requirements are
fulfilled.


8.6 Service Days

The Village would like to encourage a strong commitment to social responsibility.
By giving employees the opportunity to volunteer during company time, we are
building a sense of community and creating a work environment that is supportive
and friendly. The Village will provide 4 hours per year for full-time employees to use
for any programs that are not strictly political or religious in nature. Volunteering is
limited to organization that are tax code Section 501c3 nonprofits. Employees must
provide a written request at least one week prior to the required volunteer time.

MEMORANDUM

       To:    Members of the Village of Plain City Council
       From: Haley Lupton, Village Administrator
       Date: June 30, 2026
       RE:    Resolution 28-2026: Authorizing and Implementing the Drug Law Enforcement
              Fund Policy



Background:

In routine review of Village practices and policies, and pursuant to the direction of the Village of
Plain City’s annual audit, staff has prepared legislation for Council’s review that would implement
the Drug Law Enforcement Fund Policy. The requirement for this policy is set forth through Ohio
Revised Code Chapter 2529.03(F)(2). The implementation of the policy formalizes the process in
which funds from court-ordered mandatory drug fines may be received and expended by the
Village. The policy complies with all requirements and mandates as set forth in Ohio Revised Code
Chapter 2529.03 and includes the reporting and accounting requirements for deposits and
expenditures from the Drug Law Enforcement Fund. The final draft of the Drug Law Enforcement
Fund Policy is attached to Resolution 28-2026 in the form of Exhibit A. If approved, the Drug Law
Enforcement Fund Policy will reside within the Policy and Procedure Manual, Section 3.6.

Objective:

To approve and implement the Drug Law Enforcement Fund Policy.

Recommendation:

Staff supports and recommends the passage of Resolution 28-2026 at the second reading on
August 10, 2026. The implementation of the Drug Law Enforcement Fund Policy meets statutory
requirements and Ohio Auditor of State regulations. The policy meets all industry-standard
municipal budgeting and accounting practices.

                                                                    Drug Law Enforcement Fund Policy
                                                                                Revised _______, 2026

1. PURPOSE

The purpose of the Drug Law Enforcement Fund Policy (“Policy”) is to comply with the statutory
requirements of Ohio Revised Code Section 2529.03(F)(2) and to comply with requirements of the
Auditor of the State of Ohio. This Policy establishes the Plain City Police Department’s written
internal control policy regulating the receipt and expenditures of proceeds from court-ordered
mandatory drug fines.

2. DEFINITIONS

   A. Drug Law Enforcement Fund: Means the Drug Law Enforcement Fund of the Village of
      Plain City.

3. RESPONSIBILITY AND AUTHORITY

   A. Administrator – It is the responsibility of the Administrator to:
         (1) Ensure that the Drug Law Enforcement Fund Policy is adhered to and maintains
             updated information based on standard industry practices, the Ohio Revised Code,
             and policies of the Auditor of the State of Ohio.
   B. Chief of Police – It is the responsibility of the Chief of Police to:
         (1) Ensure that the Drug Law Enforcement Fund Policy is adhered to and maintains
             updated information based on standard industry practices, the Ohio Revised Code,
             and policies of the Auditor of the State of Ohio.
   C. Director of Finance – It is the responsibility of the Director of Finance to:
         (1) Ensure that the Drug Law Enforcement Fund Policy is adhered to and maintains
             updated information based on revenues and expenditures, including accurate
             recordkeeping in compliance with provisions of the Ohio Revised Code and this
             Policy.

4. POLICY

   A. General Procedures
         (1) Upon order of the appropriate court holding jurisdiction over qualifying drug-
             related offenses committed within the municipality, money and/or the monetary
             proceeds of mandated fines issued to the municipality shall be deposited into the
             Drug Law Enforcement Fund by the Director of Finance or designee.
         (2) Each such deposit into the Drug Law Enforcement Fund shall be properly recorded
             by the Director of Finance, or designee, using standard accounting principles and
             source documents to ensure proper future reference and/or audit compliance
             regarding the source of those funds. All supporting documentation will be
             incorporated into the municipality’s fiscal and/or audit records in conjunction with
             monitoring receipts and expenditures of the Drug Law Enforcement Fund.




                                                                                                    3


                                                              Policy & Procedure Manual Section 3.6
                                                                 Drug Law Enforcement Fund Policy
                                                                             Revised _______, 2026

B. Receipts
      (1) In addition to the above general procedures, upon the receipt of any funds issued
          pursuant to Ohio Revised Code Section 2925.03(F)(1) or 2925.03(F)(2), the Finance
          Department, in coordination with the Police Department, shall fully document the
          following:
               a. The date the funds were received.
               b. The amount of such funds.
C. Expenditures
      (1) Upon the expenditure of any funds from the Drug Law Enforcement Fund, the
          Police Department shall fully document the specific amount expended on each
          general type of expenditure.
               a. The documentation of expenditures shall include the date and amount of
                   the expenditure and the general expenditure category.
      (2) The record of such expenditures shall not provide for or permit the identification of
          any specific expenditure that is made as part of, and during the pendency of, an
          ongoing investigation.
      (3) In accordance with Ohio Revised Code Section 2925.03(F), the monies from the
          Drug Law Enforcement Fund shall be used exclusively for the purpose of
          subsidizing the Plain City Police Department’s enforcement efforts that pertain to
          drug offenses, including but not limited to, paying the costs of complex cases,
          costs of training and providing technical expertise, application toward federal
          matching funds, special equipment, or for such other purposes as recommended by
          the Chief of Police.
      (4) The Finance Department shall be responsible for the maintenance of all financial
          records related to the Drug Law Enforcement Fund.

Background:

The grant funding opportunity through the Ohio Public Works Commission (OPWC) Clean Ohio
Conservation Program, as previously described within Resolution 25-2026 and attached staff
memorandum, provides up to 75% reimbursement assistance for local government subdivisions
for eligible land acquisition or improvements projects. Staff believes this program is an excellent
opportunity to request financial assistance in order to complete the Darby Land Acquisition
Project in a fiscally responsible, efficient manner.

In addition to the authorizing legislation required by the OPWC, which is in the form of Resolution
25-2026, a resolution of support from the legislative authority is also required. The resolution of
support, which Resolution 29-2026 seeks to fulfill, provides formal action indicating the Village
Council’s support of the project and request for funding. As such, staff is requesting Council’s
approval of Resolution 29-2026 and support of the Darby Land Acquisition Project.

Objective:

To provide formal support from the Village Council, as the legislative authority of the Village of
Plain City, for the Darby Land Acquisition Project and request for funding through the OPWC
Clean Ohio Conservation Program.

Recommendation:

August 10, 2026. The acquisition of the property protects an important ecological area adjacent

to the Big Darby Creek and will provide additional public recreational opportunities for residents
and visitors.

MEMORANDUM

       To:    Members of the Village of Plain City Council
       From: Haley Lupton, Village Administrator
       Date: July 21, 2026
       RE:    Resolution 31-2026: Declaring the Intersections of Madison Way and Abby Drive and
              Madison Way and Caroline Drive to be a Three Way Stop and Authorizing the
              Installation of Traffic Control Devices



Background:

In response to concerns expressed by residents, and at the direction of the Village Council, staff
has developed legislation that would designate the intersection of Madison Way and Abby Drive,
and the intersection of Madison Way and Caroline Drive, as a three way stop. The legislation, if
approved, would authorize the installation of traffic control devices, such as stop signs, to
support the three way stop designation. Upon the conclusion of discussion by Council during the
meeting on July 13, 2026, Council, by unanimous consent, determined to proceed with legislation
that would designate the aforementioned intersections as a three way stop. If approved,
Resolution 31-2026 would formally designate the intersection of Madison Way and Abby Drive, and
the intersection of Madison Way and Caroline Drive, as a three way stop and authorize the Village
Administrator to install stop signs, and additional crosswalk striping as needed, at the
intersections. The authority for the Village Council to designate intersections as a three way stop
is set forth in the Ohio Revised Code Section 4511.65(D).

Objective:

To designate the intersection of Madison Way and Abby Drive, and the intersection of Madison
Way and Caroline Drive, as a three way stop and authorize the installation of traffic control
devices.

Recommendation:

Staff supports and recommends the passage of Resolution 31-2026 at the second reading on
August 10, 2026. The designation of the intersection as a three way stop is an appropriate and



        800 Village Boulevard | P.O. Box 167 | Plain City, OH 43064 | 614-873-3527 | plaincityohio.gov


effective response to concerns expressed by residents. The designation is expected to slow
vehicular traffic for pedestrian safety and to increase overall public safety in the area.




        800 Village Boulevard | P.O. Box 167 | Plain City, OH 43064 | 614-873-3527 | plaincityohio.gov


                                RESOLUTION NO. 31-2026

 A RESOLUTION DECLARING THE INTERSECTIONS OF MADISON WAY AND
ABBY DRIVE AND MADISON WAY AND CAROLINE DRIVE TO BE A THREE WAY
   STOP AND AUTHORIZING THE INSTALLATION OF TRAFFIC CONTROL
                           DEVICES

WHEREAS, the Village Council, as the legislative authority of the Village of Plain City, has
the authority, pursuant to Ohio Revised Code (O.R.C.) Section 4511.65(D), to designate any
intersection as a stop intersection and authorize the installation of stop signs at such
intersection; and

WHEREAS, the Village Council has considered concerns raised by residents regarding the
safety of pedestrians utilizing the designated crosswalks at the intersection of Madison
Way and Abby Drive, as well as the intersection of Madison Way and Caroline Drive, including
concerns regarding vehicular through-traffic not yielding to pedestrians in the designated
crosswalks; and

WHEREAS, the Village Council, upon review and deliberation, has determined that it is in the
best interest of public safety to designate the intersection of Madison Way and Abby Drive,
as well as the intersection of Madison Way and Caroline Drive, as a three way stop and to
authorize the installation of traffic control devices, such as stop signs, at said intersections.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the Village of Plain City, Ohio, a majority
of the members elected or appointed thereto concurring, as follows:

Section 1. The Village Council hereby designates the intersection of Madison Way and Abby
Drive, as well as the intersection of Madison Way and Caroline Drive, to be a three way stop.

Section 2. The Village Council further authorizes the installation of traffic control devices,
including stop signs, at the intersection of Madison Way and Abby Drive, as well as the
intersection of Madison Way and Caroline Drive, to effectuate the designation of said
intersection as a three way stop.

Section 3. The Village Administrator is hereby authorized and directed to take any required
subsequent action to execute the provisions of this Resolution.

Section 4. It is found that all formal actions of this Council concerning and relating to the
passage of this Resolution were adopted in an open meeting of this Council and that all
deliberations of this Council that resulted in this formal action were in meetings open to the
public in compliance with all legal requirements, including Section 121.22 of the Ohio
Revised Code.


Section 5. This Resolution shall be effective from and after the earliest period provided by
law.
