MEMORANDUM

       To:    Members of the Village of Plain City Council
       From: Haley Lupton, Village Administrator
       Date: July 23, 2026
       RE:    Resolution 32-2026: Amending Resolution 22-2026 and the Contract with
              Chemcote Inc for the 2026 Village of Plain City Resurfacing Program



Background:

Through the approval of Resolution 22-2026, the Village Council authorized the award of the
contract for the 2026 Village of Plain City Resurfacing Program to Chemcote Inc. in the amount of
$382,945.80 and authorized the Village Administrator to approve change orders up to an
additional 10% of the original award amount. Since the approval of Resolution 22-2026, the scope
of work has been amended and includes additional work that exceeds 10% of the original contract
award amount. The additional scope of work includes the resurfacing of North Chillicothe Street
from E. First Avenue to W. Second Street. This added scope of work, combined with the
previously awarded scope of work, will result in a cost-effective approach to resurface additional
roadway while maintaining fiscal responsibility. The additional scope of work is an added
$83,535.50 and will result in a new contract amount of $466,481.30. Due to the above described
additional scope of work, staff is requesting Council’s consideration in amending the contract
through the passage of Resolution 32-2026.

Objective:

To authorize the Village Administrator to amend and execute the agreement with Chemcote Inc.
to complete the 2026 Village of Plain City Resurfacing Program.

Recommendation:

Staff supports and recommends the passage of Resolution 32-2026 at the second reading on
August 10, 2026. The additional scope of work is a cost-effective approach to the project and will
support additional infrastructure improvements that will benefit vehicular traffic.




        800 Village Boulevard | P.O. Box 167 | Plain City, OH 43064 | 614-873-3527 | plaincityohio.gov

                                ORDINANCE NO. 38-2026

  AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING FOR THE ISSUANCE AND SALE OF UNVOTED
  GENERAL OBLIGATION NOTES IN THE MAXIMUM AGGREGATE PRINCIPAL
  AMOUNT OF $3,850,000, IN ANTICIPATION OF THE ISSUANCE OF BONDS,
 FOR THE PURPOSE OF PAYING THE COSTS OF VARIOUS MUNICIPAL PUBLIC
       IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS AND DECLARING AN EMERGENCY

WHEREAS, pursuant to Ordinances No. 31-2025, No, 32-2025 and No. 33-2025, each passed
August 25, 2025, notes in anticipation of bonds in the aggregate principal amount of
$3,975,000, dated September 23, 2025 (the “Outstanding Notes”), were issued for the
component purposes described in in Section 1, to mature on September 22, 2026; and

WHEREAS, the Village Council finds and determines that the Village should retire the
Outstanding Notes with the proceeds of the Notes described in Section 3 and other funds
available to the Village; and

WHEREAS, the Village Council has requested that the Director of Finance, as fiscal officer
of this Village, certify the estimated life or period of usefulness of each component purpose
of the Improvement described in Section 1, the estimated maximum maturity of the Bonds
described in Section 1 and the maximum maturity of the Notes described in Section 3 to be
issued in anticipation of the Bonds; and

WHEREAS, the Director of Finance has certified to the Village Council that the estimated
life or period of usefulness of each component purpose of the Improvement described in
Section 1 is at least five (5) years, the weighted average estimated maximum maturity of the
Bonds described in Section 1 is twenty-six (26) years, and the maximum maturity of the
Notes described in Section 3, to be issued in anticipation of the Bonds, in clause (a) of
Section 1 is October 10, 2029 for the $79,891 portion of the Notes, in clause (b) of Section 1
is May 14, 2029 for the $29,012 portion of the Notes and October 10, 2030 for the $89,177
portion of the Notes, in clause (c) of Section 1 is May 16, 2037 for the $142,323 portion of the
Notes, May 14, 2038 for the $148,923 portion of the Notes and October 10, 2039 for the
$86,351 portion of the Notes, in clause (d) of Section 1 is May 16, 2037 for the $172,813 portion
of the Notes and October 10, 2039 for the $18,546 portion of the Notes, in clause (e) of
Section 1 is May 14, 2028 for the $71,690 portion of the Notes and October 10, 2029 for the
$11,274 portion of the Notes, in clause (f) of Section 1 is October 31, 2043 for the $450,000
portion of the Notes, in clause (g) of Section 1 is September 23, 2045 for the $1,550,000
portion of the Notes and in clause (h) of Section 1 is September 23, 2045 for the $1,000,000
portion of the Notes.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED by the Council of the Village of Plain City, Ohio, a majority
of the members elected or appointed thereto concurring, as follows:


Section 1. It is necessary to issue bonds of this Village in the maximum aggregate principal
amount of $3,850,000 (the “Bonds”) for the purpose of paying the costs of (a) constructing,
furnishing, equipping and improving municipal facilities, together with related site
improvements and all necessary appurtenances thereto, (b) acquiring, constructing,
expanding, repairing, rehabilitating and otherwise improving the municipal sewer system,
together with all necessary appurtenances thereto, (c) constructing, reconstructing and
paving streets and related public infrastructure, together with all necessary appurtenances
thereto, (d) acquiring, constructing, expanding, repairing, rehabilitating and otherwise
improving the municipal water system, together with all necessary appurtenances thereto,
(e) acquiring vehicles and related equipment for Village purposes, together with all
necessary appurtenances thereto, (f) constructing storm water improvements along
Noteman Road, together with all necessary appurtenances thereto, (g) improving the
municipal park system by acquiring real estate to be used for constructing open gathering
places and public parking, together with all necessary appurtenances thereto and (h)
acquiring real estate to be used for municipal purposes, together with all necessary
appurtenances thereto (collectively, the “Improvement”).

Section 2. The Bonds shall be dated approximately September 1, 2027, shall bear interest at
the now estimated rate of 6.00% per year, payable semiannually until the principal amount
is paid, and are estimated to mature in twenty (20) annual principal installments on
December 1 of each year and in such amounts that the total principal and interest payments
on the Bonds, in any fiscal year in which principal is payable, shall be substantially equal.
The first principal payment of the Bonds is estimated to be December 1, 2027.

Section 3. It is necessary to issue and this Council determines that notes in the maximum
aggregate principal amount of $3,850,000 (the “Notes”) shall be issued in anticipation of the
issuance of the Bonds for the component purposes described in Section 1 and to retire,
together with other funds available to the Village, the Outstanding Notes and to pay any
financing costs. The aggregate principal amount of Notes to be issued (not to exceed the
aggregate of the maximum amount for each component purpose) shall be determined by
the Director of Finance in the certificate awarding the Notes in accordance with Section 6
of this Ordinance (the “Certificate of Award”) as the amount which, along with other available
funds of the Village, is necessary to provide for the retirement of the Outstanding Notes and
to pay any financing costs. The Notes shall be dated the date of issuance and shall mature
not more than one year following the date of issuance, provided that the Director of Finance
shall establish the maturity date in the Certificate of Award. The Notes shall bear interest
at a rate or rates not to exceed 6.00% per year (computed on the basis of a 360-day year
consisting of twelve 30-day months), payable at maturity and until the principal amount is
paid or payment is provided for. The rate or rates of interest on the Notes shall be
determined by the Director of Finance in the Certificate of Award in accordance with
Section 6 of this Ordinance.

Section 4. The debt charges on the Notes shall be payable in lawful money of the United
States of America or in Federal Reserve funds of the United States of America as
determined by the Director of Finance in the Certificate of Award, and shall be payable,


without deduction for services of the Village’s paying agent, at the office of a bank or trust
company designated by the Director of Finance in the Certificate of Award after
determining that the payment at that bank or trust company will not endanger the funds or
securities of the Village and that proper procedures and safeguards are available for that
purpose or at the office of the Director of Finance if agreed to by the Director of Finance
and the original purchaser (the “Paying Agent”).

The Administrator and the Director of Finance shall sign and deliver, in the name and on
behalf of the Village, the Note Registrar Agreement between the Village and the Paying
Agent, in substantially the form as is now on file with the Clerk of Council. The Note
Registrar Agreement is approved, together with any changes or amendments that are not
inconsistent with this Ordinance and not substantially adverse to the Village and that are
approved by the Administrator and the Director of Finance on behalf of the Village, all of
which shall be conclusively evidenced by the signing of the Note Registrar Agreement or
amendments thereto. The Director of Finance shall provide for the payment of the services
rendered and for reimbursement of expenses incurred pursuant to the Note Registrar
Agreement, except to the extent paid or reimbursed by the original purchaser in accordance
with the Note Purchase Agreement and/or the Certificate of Award, from the proceeds of
the Notes to the extent available and then from other money lawfully available and
appropriated or to be appropriated for that purpose.

Section 5. The Notes shall be signed by the Administrator and the Director of Finance, in the
name of the Village and in their official capacities; provided that one of those signatures
may be a facsimile. The Notes shall be issued in minimum denominations of $100,000 (and
may be issued in denominations in such amounts in excess thereof as requested by the
original purchaser and approved by the Director of Finance) and with numbers as requested
by the original purchaser and approved by the Director of Finance. The entire principal
amount may be represented by a single note and may be issued as fully registered securities
(for which the Director of Finance will serve as note registrar) and in book entry or other
uncertificated form in accordance with Section 9.96 and Chapter 133 of the Ohio Revised
Code if it is determined by the Director of Finance that issuance of fully registered
securities in that form will facilitate the sale and delivery of the Notes. The Notes shall not
have coupons attached, shall be numbered as determined by the Director of Finance and
shall express upon their faces the purpose, in summary terms, for which they are issued and
that they are issued pursuant to this Ordinance. As used in this Section and this Ordinance:

“Book entry form” or “book entry system” means a form or system under which (a) the
ownership of beneficial interests in the Notes and the principal of and interest on the Notes
may be transferred only through a book entry, and (b) a single physical Note certificate in
fully registered form is issued by the Village and payable only to a Depository or its nominee
as registered owner, with the certificate deposited with and “immobilized” in the custody of
the Depository or its designated agent for that purpose. The book entry maintained by
others than the Village is the record that identifies the owners of beneficial interests in the
Notes and that principal and interest.


“Depository” means any securities depository that is a clearing agency registered pursuant
to the provisions of Section 17A of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, operating and
maintaining, with its Participants or otherwise, a book entry system to record ownership of
beneficial interests in the Notes or the principal of and interest on the Notes, and to effect
transfers of the Notes, in book entry form, and includes and means initially The Depository
Trust Company (a limited purpose trust company).

“Participant” means any participant contracting with a Depository under a book entry
system and includes securities brokers and dealers, banks and trust companies and
clearing corporations.

The Notes may be issued to a Depository for use in a book entry system and, if and as long
as a book entry system is utilized, (a) the Notes may be issued in the form of a single Note
made payable to the Depository or its nominee and immobilized in the custody of the
Depository or its agent for that purpose; (b) the beneficial owners in book entry form shall
have no right to receive the Notes in the form of physical securities or certificates; (c)
ownership of beneficial interests in book entry form shall be shown by book entry on the
system maintained and operated by the Depository and its Participants, and transfers of the
ownership of beneficial interests shall be made only by book entry by the Depository and its
Participants; and (d) the Notes as such shall not be transferable or exchangeable, except for
transfer to another Depository or to another nominee of a Depository, without further action
by the Village.

If any Depository determines not to continue to act as a Depository for the Notes for use in
a book entry system, the Director of Finance may attempt to establish a securities
depository/book entry relationship with another qualified Depository. If the Director of
Finance does not or is unable to do so, the Director of Finance, after making provision for
notification of the beneficial owners by the then Depository and any other arrangements
deemed necessary, shall permit withdrawal of the Notes from the Depository, and shall
cause the Notes in bearer or payable form to be signed by the officers authorized to sign the
Notes and delivered to the assigns of the Depository or its nominee, all at the cost and
expense (including any costs of printing), if the event is not the result of Village action or
inaction, of those persons requesting such issuance.

The Director of Finance is also hereby authorized and directed, to the extent necessary or
required, to enter into any agreements determined necessary in connection with the book
entry system for the Notes, after determining that the signing thereof will not endanger the
funds or securities of the Village.

Section 6. The Notes shall be sold at not less than par plus accrued interest (if any) at private
sale by the Director of Finance in accordance with law and the provisions of this Ordinance.
The Director of Finance shall sign the Certificate of Award referred to in Section 3 fixing the
interest rate or rates which the Notes shall bear and evidencing that sale to the original
purchaser, cause the Notes to be prepared, and have the Notes signed and delivered,
together with a true transcript of proceedings with reference to the issuance of the Notes


if requested by the original purchaser, to the original purchaser upon payment of the
purchase price.

The Note Purchase Agreement between the Village and the original purchaser and now on
file with the Clerk of Council is approved, and the Administrator and the Director of Finance
are authorized to sign and deliver, on behalf of the Village, the Note Purchase Agreement
with such changes that are not inconsistent with the provisions of this Ordinance, are not
materially adverse to the interests of the Village and are approved by the Administrator and
the Director of Finance. Any such changes to the Note Purchase Agreement are not
materially adverse to the interests of the Village and are approved by the Administrator and
the Director of Finance shall be evidenced conclusively by the signing of the Note Purchase
Agreement by the Administrator and the Director of Finance.

The Mayor, the Administrator, the Director of Finance, the Director of Law, the Clerk of
Council and other Village officials, as appropriate, and any person serving in an interim or
acting capacity for any such official, are each authorized and directed to sign any transcript
certificates, financial statements and other documents and instruments and to take such
actions as are necessary or appropriate to consummate the transactions contemplated by
this Ordinance. Any actions heretofore taken by the Mayor, the Administrator, the Director
of Finance, the Director of Law, the Clerk of Council or other Village official, as appropriate,
in doing any and all acts necessary in connection with the issuance and sale of the Notes are
hereby ratified and confirmed. The Director of Finance is authorized, if it is determined to
be in the best interest of the Village, to combine the issue of Notes with one or more other
note issues of the Village into a consolidated note issue pursuant to Section 133.30(B) of the
Ohio Revised Code.

To the extent that the Director of Finance determines that it would be in the best interest
of the Village and elects to utilize the Ohio Market Access Program (the “Ohio Market Access
Program”) which is administered by the Treasurer of the State of Ohio (the “Treasurer”), the
Administrator and the Director of Finance are authorized to sign and deliver, in the name
and on behalf of the Village, the Standby Note Purchase Agreement (the “Standby Note
Purchase Agreement”) in substantially the form as presented to this Village Council with
such changes as are not materially adverse to the Village and as may be approved by the
officers of the Village executing the Standby Note Purchase Agreement. The Village
acknowledges the agreement of the Treasurer in the Standby Note Purchase Agreement
that, in the event the Village is unable to repay the principal amount and accrued and unpaid
interest of the Notes at their maturity, whether through its own funds or through the
issuance of other obligations of the Village, the Treasurer agrees to (a) purchase the Notes
from the holders or beneficial owners thereof upon their presentation to the Treasurer for
such purchase at a price of par plus accrued interest to maturity or (b) purchase renewal
notes of the Village in a principal amount not greater than the principal amount of the Notes
plus interest due at maturity, with such renewal notes bearing interest at the Renewal Note
Rate (as defined in the Standby Note Purchase Agreement), maturing not more than one
year after the date of their issuance, and being prepayable at any time with 30 days’ notice,
provided that in connection with the Treasurer’s purchase of such renewal notes the Village


shall deliver to the Treasurer an unqualified opinion of nationally recognized bond counsel
that (i) such renewal notes are the legal, valid and binding general obligations of the Village,
and the principal of and interest on such renewal notes, unless paid from other sources, are
to be paid from the proceeds of the levy of ad valorem taxes, within the ten-mill limitation
imposed by law, on all property subject to ad valorem taxes levied by the Village and (ii)
interest on the renewal notes is excluded from gross income for federal income tax
purposes under Section 103 of the Internal Revenue Code, as amended, to the same extent
that interest on the Notes is so excluded.

The officers signing the Notes are authorized to take all actions that may in their judgment
reasonably be necessary to provide for the Standby Note Purchase Agreement, including
but not limited to the inclusion of a notation on the form of the Notes providing notice to the
holders or beneficial owners of the existence of the Standby Note Purchase Agreement and
providing instructions to such holders or beneficial owners regarding the presentation of
the Note for purchase by the Treasurer at stated maturity.

Section 7. The proceeds from the sale of the Notes received by the Village (or withheld by
the original purchaser or deposited with the Paying Agent, in each case on behalf of the
Village) shall be paid into the proper fund or funds, and those proceeds are appropriated and
shall be used for the purpose for which the Notes are being issued. The Certificate of Award
and/or the Note Purchase Agreement may authorize the original purchaser to (a) withhold
certain proceeds from the sale of the Notes or (b) remit certain proceeds from the sale of
the Notes to the Paying Agent, in each case to provide for the payment of certain financing
costs on behalf of the Village. If proceeds are remitted to the Paying Agent in accordance
with this Section 7, the Paying Agent shall be authorized to create a fund in accordance with
the Note Registrar Agreement for that purpose. Any portion of those proceeds received by
the Village (after payment of those financing costs) representing premium or accrued
interest shall be paid into the Bond Retirement Fund.

Section 8. The par value to be received from the sale of the Bonds or of any renewal notes
and any excess funds resulting from the issuance of the Notes shall, to the extent
necessary, be used to pay the debt charges on the Notes at maturity and are pledged for
that purpose.

Section 9. During the year or years in which the Notes are outstanding, there shall be levied
on all the taxable property in the Village, in addition to all other taxes, the same tax that
would have been levied if the Bonds had been issued without the prior issuance of the
Notes. The tax shall be within the ten mill limitation imposed by law, shall be and is ordered
computed, certified, levied and extended upon the tax duplicate and collected by the same
officers, in the same manner, and at the same time that taxes for general purposes for each
of those years are certified, levied, extended and collected, and shall be placed before and
in preference to all other items and for the full amount thereof. The proceeds of the tax levy
shall be placed in the Bond Retirement Fund, which is irrevocably pledged for the payment
of the debt charges on the Notes or the Bonds when and as the same fall due.


In each year to the extent receipts from the municipal income tax are available for the
payment of the debt charges on the Notes or the Bonds and are appropriated for that
purpose, the amount of the tax shall be reduced by the amount of such receipts so available
and appropriated in compliance with the following covenant. To the extent necessary, the
debt charges on the Notes or the Bonds shall be paid from municipal income taxes lawfully
available therefor under the Constitution and the laws of the State of Ohio and the Charter
of the Village; and the Village hereby covenants, subject and pursuant to such authority,
including particularly Section 133.05(B)(7) of the Ohio Revised Code, to appropriate annually
from such municipal income taxes such amount as is necessary to meet such annual debt
charges.

Nothing in the preceding paragraph in any way diminishes the irrevocable pledge of the full
faith and credit and general property taxing power of the Village to the prompt payment of
the debt charges on the Notes or the Bonds.

Section 10. The Village covenants that it will use, and will restrict the use and investment of,
the proceeds of the Notes in such manner and to such extent as may be necessary so that
(a) the Notes will not (i) constitute private activity bonds or arbitrage bonds under Sections
141 or 148 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “Code”) or (ii) be treated
other than as bonds the interest on which is excluded from gross income under Section 103
of the Code, and (b) the interest on the Notes will not be an item of tax preference under
Section 57 of the Code.

The Village further covenants that (a) it will take or cause to be taken such actions that may
be required of it for the interest on the Notes to be and remain excluded from gross income
for federal income tax purposes, (b) it will not take or authorize to be taken any actions that
would adversely affect that exclusion, and (c) it, or persons acting for it, will, among other
acts of compliance, (i) apply the proceeds of the Notes to the governmental purpose of the
borrowing, (ii) restrict the yield on investment property, (iii) make timely and adequate
payments to the federal government, (iv) maintain books and records and make calculations
and reports and (v) refrain from certain uses of those proceeds, and, as applicable, of
property financed with such proceeds, all in such manner and to the extent necessary to
assure such exclusion of that interest under the Code.

The Director of Finance or any other officer of the Village having responsibility for issuance
of the Notes is hereby authorized (a) to make or effect any election, selection, designation,
choice, consent, approval, or waiver on behalf of the Village with respect to the Notes as the
Village is permitted to or required to make or give under the federal income tax laws,
including, without limitation thereto, any of the elections available under Section 148 of the
Code, for the purpose of assuring, enhancing or protecting favorable tax treatment or
status of the Notes or interest thereon or assisting compliance with requirements for that
purpose, reducing the burden or expense of such compliance, reducing the rebate amount
or payments or penalties with respect to the Notes, or making payments of special amounts
in lieu of making computations to determine, or paying, excess earnings as rebate, or
obviating those amounts or payments with respect to the Notes, which action shall be in


writing and signed by the officer, (b) to take any and all other actions, make or obtain
calculations, make payments, and make or give reports, covenants and certifications of and
on behalf of the Village, as may be appropriate to assure the exclusion of interest from gross
income and the intended tax status of the Notes, and (c) to give one or more appropriate
certificates of the Village, for inclusion in the transcript of proceedings for the Notes,
setting forth the reasonable expectations of the Village regarding the amount and use of all
the proceeds of the Notes, the facts, circumstances and estimates on which they are based,
and other facts and circumstances relevant to the tax treatment of the interest on and the
tax status of the Notes. The Director of Finance or any other officer of the Village having
responsibility for issuance of the Notes is specifically authorized to designate the Notes as
“qualified tax-exempt obligations” if such designation is applicable and desirable, and to
make any related necessary representations and covenants.

Each covenant made in this Section with respect to the Notes is also made with respect to
all issues any portion of the debt service on which is paid from proceeds of the Notes (and,
if different, the original issue and any refunding issues in a series of refundings), to the
extent such compliance is necessary to assure the exclusion of interest on the Notes from
gross income for federal income tax purposes, and the officers identified above are
authorized to take actions with respect to those issues as they are authorized in this Section
to take with respect to the Notes.

Section 11. The Director of Finance is authorized to request a rating for the Notes from
Moody’s Ratings or S&P Global Ratings, or both, as the Director of Finance determines is in
the best interest of the Village. The expenditure of the amounts necessary to secure any
such ratings as well as to pay the other financing costs (as defined in Section 133.01 of the
Ohio Revised Code) in connection with the Notes is hereby authorized and approved and the
amounts necessary to pay those costs are hereby appropriated from the proceeds of the
Notes, if available, and otherwise from available moneys in the General Fund.

Section 12. The legal services of the law firm of Squire Patton Boggs (US) LLP, as bond
counsel, are hereby retained. Those legal services shall be in the nature of legal advice and
recommendations as to the documents and the proceedings in connection with the
authorization, sale and issuance of the Notes and securities issued in renewal of the Notes
and rendering at delivery related legal opinions, all as set forth in the form of engagement
letter from that firm which is now on file in the office of the Clerk of Council. In providing
those legal services, as an independent contractor and in an attorney-client relationship,
that firm shall not exercise any administrative discretion on behalf of this Village in the
formulation of public policy, expenditure of public funds, enforcement of laws, rules and
regulations of the State of Ohio, any county or municipal corporation or of this Village, or the
execution of public trusts. For those legal services, that firm shall be paid just and
reasonable compensation and shall be reimbursed for actual out-of-pocket expenses
incurred in providing those legal services. To the extent they are not paid or reimbursed
pursuant to the Note Purchase Agreement and/or the Note Registrar Agreement, the
Director of Finance is authorized and directed to make appropriate certification as to the
availability of funds for those fees and any reimbursement and to issue an appropriate order


for their timely payment as written statements are submitted by that firm. The amounts
necessary to pay those fees and any reimbursement are hereby appropriated from the
proceeds of the Notes, if available, and otherwise from available moneys in the General
Fund.

Section 13. The services of Rockmill Financial Consulting, LLC, as municipal advisor, are
hereby retained. The municipal advisory services shall be in the nature of financial advice
and recommendations in connection with the issuance and sale of the Notes. In rendering
those municipal advisory services, as an independent contractor, that firm shall not
exercise any administrative discretion on behalf of the Village in the formulation of public
policy, expenditure of public funds, enforcement of laws, rules and regulations of the State
of Ohio, the Village or any other political subdivision, or the execution of public trusts. That
firm shall be paid just and reasonable compensation for those municipal advisory services
and shall be reimbursed for the actual out-of-pocket expenses it incurs in rendering those
municipal advisory services. To the extent they are not paid or reimbursed pursuant to the
Note Purchase Agreement and/or the Note Registrar Agreement, the Director of Finance is
authorized and directed to make appropriate certification as to the availability of funds for
those fees and any reimbursement and to issue an appropriate order for their timely
payment as written statements are submitted by that firm. The amounts necessary to pay
those fees and any reimbursement are hereby appropriated from the proceeds of the Notes,
if available, and otherwise from available moneys in the General Fund.

Section 14. The Director of Finance is directed to promptly deliver or cause to be delivered
a certified copy of this Ordinance to the County Auditors of Madison and Union Counties,
Ohio.

Section 15. This Council determines that all acts and conditions necessary to be done or
performed by the Village or to have been met precedent to and in the issuing of the Notes in
order to make them legal, valid and binding general obligations of the Village have been
performed and have been met, or will at the time of delivery of the Notes have been
performed and have been met, in regular and due form as required by law; that the full faith
and credit and general property taxing power (as described in Section 9) of the Village are
pledged for the timely payment of the debt charges on the Notes; and that no statutory or
constitutional limitation of indebtedness or taxation will have been exceeded in the
issuance of the Notes.

Section 16. This legislation is hereby declared to be an emergency measure necessary for
the immediate preservation of the public peace, health, safety, and welfare of the Village of
Plain City and its inhabitants, and further provided it receives the affirmative vote of five
members elected to Council, it shall take effect and be in force from and after the earliest
period provided by law.

Section 17. It is found that all formal actions of this Council concerning and relating to the
passage of this Ordinance were adopted in an open meeting of this Council and that all
deliberations of this Council that resulted in this formal action were in meetings open to the


public in compliance with all legal requirements, including Section 121.22 of the Ohio
Revised Code.

Section 18. This Ordinance shall be effective from and after the earliest period provided by
law.

MEMORANDUM

       To:    Members of the Village of Plain City Council
       From: Haley Lupton, Village Administrator
       Date: July 28, 2026
       RE:    Resolution 33-2026: Accepting Public Improvements Constructed for Madison
              Meadows, Section 2A and 2B



Background:

The Village of Plain City requires, in its Subdivision Regulations of the Codified Ordinances, that
certain public improvements such as roadways, street lighting, and water and sewer
infrastructure be constructed and installed within any new subdivision. Once such improvements
are built to the satisfaction of the Village Engineer and staff, Council may choose to accept the
public improvements. Once accepted, the maintenance responsibilities of the improvements are
transferred to the Village. Resolution 33-2026 formally accepts the constructed public
improvements within the Madison Meadows, Section 2A and 2B subdivision. All improvements
have met applicable requirements and regulations and have been deemed by staff to be in such
condition that warrants acceptance.

Objective:

To formally accept the public improvements constructed in the Madison Meadows, Section 2A
and 2B subdivision.

Recommendation:

Staff supports and recommends the passage of Resolution 33-2026 at the second reading on
August 24, 2026. The acceptance of public improvements is in accordance with standard Village
policy and regulations in regards to developmental procedures. The public improvements have
been thoroughly inspected and have met all applicable requirements.




        800 Village Boulevard | P.O. Box 167 | Plain City, OH 43064 | 614-873-3527 | plaincityohio.gov


                              RESOLUTION NO. 33-2026

  A RESOLUTION ACCEPTING PUBLIC IMPROVEMENTS CONSTRUCTED FOR
              MADISON MEADOWS, SECTION 2A AND 2B

WHEREAS, the Village of Plain City’s Subdivision Regulations within Chapter 1125 of the
Codified Ordinances require the installation of certain public improvements for all
subdivisions within the Village; and

WHEREAS, the developer of Section 2A and 2B of the Madison Meadows subdivision has
installed such required improvements in accordance with the record plan and
accompanying public improvement plans previously approved by the Village Council; and

WHEREAS, the Village Engineer and staff have inspected said public improvements and
have found them to be installed in accordance with all applicable construction regulations
and requirements of the Village; and

WHEREAS, the developer of Section 2A and 2B of the Madison Meadows subdivision desires
to dedicate said public improvements to the Village and to the benefit of the public for the
future; and

WHEREAS, the Village Council has determined that the public improvements within Section
2A and 2B of the Madison Meadows subdivision, as identified in Exhibit A attached hereto
and incorporated herein, should be accepted and the acceptance of such public
improvements is in the best interests of the Village of Plain City and residents.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the Village of Plain City, Ohio, a majority
of the members elected or appointed thereto concurring, as follows:

Section 1. The Village Council hereby accepts the dedication of the public improvements for
Section 2A and 2B of the Madison Meadows subdivision, as identified in Exhibit A attached
hereto and incorporated herein, all in accordance with Chapter 1129 of the Village of Plain
City Codified Ordinances.

Section 2. In accordance with the provisions of Section 1 of this Resolution, the release of
the maintenance bond in the amount of $244,000.00 is hereby authorized.

Section 3. The Village Administrator is hereby authorized and directed to take any required
subsequent action to execute the release the maintenance bond in accordance with the
provisions of this Resolution.

Section 4. It is found that all formal actions of this Council concerning and relating to the
passage of this Resolution were adopted in an open meeting of this Council and that all
deliberations of this Council that resulted in this formal action were in meetings open to the


public in compliance with all legal requirements, including Section 121.22 of the Ohio
Revised Code.

Section 5. This Resolution shall be effective from and after the earliest period provided by
law.

MEMORANDUM

       To:    Members of the Village of Plain City Council
       From: Haley Lupton, Village Administrator
       Date: July 28, 2026
       RE:    Resolution 34-2026: Accepting Public Improvements Constructed for Madison
              Meadows, Section 1



Background:

The Village of Plain City requires, in its Subdivision Regulations of the Codified Ordinances, that
certain public improvements such as roadways, street lighting, and water and sewer
infrastructure be constructed and installed within any new subdivision. Once such improvements
are built to the satisfaction of the Village Engineer and staff, Council may choose to accept the
public improvements. Once accepted, the maintenance responsibilities of the improvements are
transferred to the Village. Resolution 34-2026 formally accepts the constructed public
improvements within the Madison Meadows, Section 1 subdivision. All improvements have met
applicable requirements and regulations and have been deemed by staff to be in such condition
that warrants acceptance.

Objective:

To formally accept the public improvements constructed in the Madison Meadows, Section 1
subdivision.

Recommendation:

Staff supports and recommends the passage of Resolution 34-2026 at the second reading on
August 24, 2026. The acceptance of public improvements is in accordance with standard Village
policy and regulations in regards to developmental procedures. The public improvements have
been thoroughly inspected and have met all applicable requirements.




        800 Village Boulevard | P.O. Box 167 | Plain City, OH 43064 | 614-873-3527 | plaincityohio.gov


                              RESOLUTION NO. 34-2026

  A RESOLUTION ACCEPTING PUBLIC IMPROVEMENTS CONSTRUCTED FOR
                  MADISON MEADOWS, SECTION 1

WHEREAS, the Village of Plain City’s Subdivision Regulations within Chapter 1125 of the
Codified Ordinances require the installation of certain public improvements for all
subdivisions within the Village; and

WHEREAS, the developer of Section 1 of the Madison Meadows subdivision has installed
such required improvements in accordance with the record plan and accompanying public
improvement plans previously approved by the Village Council; and

WHEREAS, the Village Engineer and staff have inspected said public improvements and
have found them to be installed in accordance with all applicable construction regulations
and requirements of the Village; and

WHEREAS, the developer of Section 1 of the Madison Meadows subdivision desires to
dedicate said public improvements to the Village and to the benefit of the public for the
future; and

WHEREAS, the Village Council has determined that the public improvements within Section
1 of the Madison Meadows subdivision, as identified in Exhibit A attached hereto and
incorporated herein, should be accepted and the acceptance of such public improvements
is in the best interests of the Village of Plain City and residents.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the Village of Plain City, Ohio, a majority
of the members elected or appointed thereto concurring, as follows:

Section 1. The Village Council hereby accepts the dedication of the public improvements for
Section 1 of the Madison Meadows subdivision, as identified in Exhibit A attached hereto and
incorporated herein, all in accordance with Chapter 1129 of the Village of Plain City Codified
Ordinances.

Section 2. In accordance with the provisions of Section 1 of this Resolution, the release of
the maintenance bond in the amount of $404,680.00 is hereby authorized.

Section 3. The Village Administrator is hereby authorized and directed to take any required
subsequent action to execute the release the maintenance bond in accordance with the
provisions of this Resolution.

Section 4. It is found that all formal actions of this Council concerning and relating to the
passage of this Resolution were adopted in an open meeting of this Council and that all
deliberations of this Council that resulted in this formal action were in meetings open to the


public in compliance with all legal requirements, including Section 121.22 of the Ohio
Revised Code.

Section 5. This Resolution shall be effective from and after the earliest period provided by
law.

MEMORANDUM

       To:    Members of the Village of Plain City Council
       From: Haley Lupton, Village Administrator
       Date: July 28, 2026
       RE:    Resolution 35-2026: Accepting Public Improvements Constructed for Madison
              Meadows, Section 3A and 3B



Background:

The Village of Plain City requires, in its Subdivision Regulations of the Codified Ordinances, that
certain public improvements such as roadways, street lighting, and water and sewer
infrastructure be constructed and installed within any new subdivision. Once such improvements
are built to the satisfaction of the Village Engineer and staff, Council may choose to accept the
public improvements. Once accepted, the maintenance responsibilities of the improvements are
transferred to the Village. Resolution 35-2026 formally accepts the constructed public
improvements within the Madison Meadows, Section 3A and 3B subdivision. All improvements
have met applicable requirements and regulations and have been deemed by staff to be in such
condition that warrants acceptance.

Objective:

To formally accept the public improvements constructed in the Madison Meadows, Section 3A
and 3B subdivision.

Recommendation:

Staff supports and recommends the passage of Resolution 35-2026 at the second reading on
August 24, 2026. The acceptance of public improvements is in accordance with standard Village
policy and regulations in regards to developmental procedures. The public improvements have
been thoroughly inspected and have met all applicable requirements.

MEMORANDUM

       To:    Members of the Village of Plain City Council
       From: Haley Lupton, Village Administrator
       Date: July 22, 2026
       RE:    Resolution 36-2026: Adopting the Village of Plain City’s Engineering Design
              Standards



Background:

On April 27, 2026, the Village Council approved Ordinance 12-2026, which enacted Chapter 1124 of
the Codified Ordinances and is titled “Engineering Design Standards for Improvements”. The
enactment of Chapter 1124 was completed in order to set forth the authority for the
implementation of the Village of Plain City Engineering Design Standards (the “Engineering
Design Standards”). The Engineering Design Standards, in conjunction with the provisions of
Chapter 1124, establishes the requirements for the design, construction, and installation of public
and private infrastructure and improvements as part of the development process. With the
conclusion of the thirty day effective period for Ordinance 12-2026, Council may now formally
adopt the Engineering Design Standards through the passage of a Resolution, in accordance with
the provisions of Chapter 1124.02. The Village Council reviewed the Engineering Design Standards
during its meeting on March 9, 2026. The finalized Engineering Design Standards is attached to
Resolution 36-2026 in the form of Exhibit A.

Objective:

To adopt the Village of Plain City Engineering Design Standards.

Recommendation:

Staff supports and recommends the passage of Resolution 36-2026 at the second reading on
August 24, 2026. The Engineering Design Standards has been created through extensive
research and discussion. Furthermore, the Engineering Design Standards provides an important
foundation and regulatory framework for the design, construction, and installation of
improvements and infrastructure within the land development process.



        800 Village Boulevard | P.O. Box 167 | Plain City, OH 43064 | 614-873-3527 | plaincityohio.gov


                              RESOLUTION NO. 36-2026

   A RESOLUTION ADOPTING THE VILLAGE OF PLAIN CITY’S ENGINEERING
                       DESIGN STANDARDS

WHEREAS, the Village of Plain City Council desires to maintain uniform requirements for
the design, construction, and installation of public and private improvements in regards to
the subdivision of land and land development within the Village of Plain City; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to the provisions of Ordinance 12-2026, Chapter 1124 of the Codified
Ordinances, titled “Engineering Design Standards for Improvements”, has been enacted and
such enactment requires the adoption of the Village of Plain City Engineering Design
Standards (the “Engineering Design Standards”) in order to set forth the requirements for
the design, construction, and installation of public and private improvements as part of the
land development process; and

WHEREAS, the Village Council has reviewed the Engineering Design Standards and has
determined that the adoption and implementation of the Engineering Design Standards is
in the best interests of the Village of Plain City and its residents; and

WHEREAS, the Village Council has determined that the Engineering Design Standards, as
shown in Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein, be adopted in accordance with
the provisions of Chapter 1124 of the Codified Ordinances.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the Village of Plain City, Ohio, a majority
of the members elected or appointed thereto concurring, as follows:

Section 1. The Village Council hereby approves and authorizes the adoption and
implementation of the Engineering Design Standards, as identified in Exhibit A, and
attached hereto and incorporated herein.

Section 2. The Village Administrator is hereby authorized and directed to take any required
subsequent action, in accordance with the responsibilities and authority set forth in the
Plain City Charter, to implement the Engineering Design Standards.

Section 3. It is found that all formal actions of this Council concerning and relating to the
passage of this Resolution were adopted in an open meeting of this Council and that all
deliberations of this Council that resulted in this formal action were in meetings open to the
public in compliance with all legal requirements, including Section 121.22 of the Ohio
Revised Code.

Section 4. This Resolution shall be effective from and after the earliest period provided by
law.

Section 1 – Review Procedures
1) General Considerations

   a) Anyone wishing to develop land within the Village is required to submit engineering
      plans and calculations to the Village for their approval prior to construction.
   b) Development is defined as any man-made change to improved or unimproved real
      estate, including but not limited to buildings or other structures, mining, dredging, filling,
      grading, paving, excavation, or drilling operations.
   c) All engineering plans, calculations, and reports shall be prepared, signed, and sealed by
      a professional engineer registered in the State of Ohio.
   d) The latest edition of the City of Columbus, Ohio Construction and Material Specifications
      and Standard Drawings shall govern all required improvements, except as modified
      within these Design Standards and the Village’s Standard Drawings found in Appendix
      D.
   e) The Village’s Standard Drawing library is incorporated into these Design Standards and
      shall govern the construction of their respective items.
   f)   Improvement plans and calculations shall be submitted electronically to the Village via
        PDF. Freehand linear drawings will not be accepted. A poorly drawn or illegible plan is
        sufficient cause for rejection. Shading or coloring is discouraged unless part of an
        illustration where color may add necessary details.
   g) The sheets upon which the construction drawings are made shall measure 22" x 34",
      with ½" margin border on three sides and a 1½" to 2" binding margin on the short left
      side.
   h) Revisions to plans after approval shall clearly show all revisions made thereto by notes
      in the "revision" block and outlines of the revisions. These revisions must be approved
      by the Village prior to construction
   i)   The plan review process is outlined within the flow chart on the next page. The required
        submittal items for each step are the minimum necessary for the review of engineering
        details to take place. Refer to the zoning code and other Village guidance for additional
        items required within each step.
   j)   Fees are required to be paid by the developer to support the review of each submission.
        Fee amounts are established within the Engineering Review Fee Schedule in Appendix
        C. Separate zoning review fees may apply depending on the type of submission.
   k) The fee schedule in Appendix C is required to be completed and submitted with the first
      submission of each plan set for the Village’s approval. A fillable Excel copy of this
      schedule may be found on the Village’s application portal.
   l)   Upon the Village’s approval, these review fees must be paid in full before the Village’s
        review can begin.


Engineering Design Standards                                                                  Page 5
Village of Plain City, Ohio


                               Plan Review Process


Engineering Design Standards                         Page 6
Village of Plain City, Ohio


2) Preliminary Development Plan
Items submitted during the Preliminary Development Plan process will receive a high-level
review of engineering-related items including site layout, pedestrian and vehicular circulation
and access, drainage, and other items of concern to the Village. The details submitted shall thus
show:

   a) Proposed site layout.

   b) Existing and proposed sidewalks.

   c) Access points to public streets.

   d) Right-of-way and public street widths.

   e) Proposed stormwater runoff discharge points and detention basin locations.



3) Final Development Plan
Engineering items required within the Final Development Plan application shall provide more
advanced details of the overall site, utility, traffic, drainage, and property right improvements
necessary for the development to take place. As such, the following items are required:

   a) A site plan showing:

       i)   Right-of-way line, centerline, lot lines, lot numbers, easements, street names,
            development limits, and limits of construction.
       ii) All proposed improvements and any modifications to existing public infrastructure.
   b) A preliminary utility plan showing existing and proposed utilities and their sizes.

       Note: Coordination with the Mid-Ohio Water and Sewer District on the establishment of
       water and sewer service to the development is highly recommended ahead of this
       submission.

   c) A preliminary grading plan showing:

       i)   Proposed and existing contours

       ii) Ditches and/or channels

       iii) Overall drainage patterns

       iv) Stormwater control measures

       v) Discharge points




Engineering Design Standards                                                                  Page 7
Village of Plain City, Ohio


   d) A Preliminary Storm Water Study that includes:

       i)   An overall narrative of how stormwater runoff is managed throughout the site. This
            includes an acknowledgement of the additional requirements established by
            Appendix A of the Ohio EPA’s General Permit OHC000006 for projects within the
            watershed of the Big Darby Creek, and a description of how these requirements will
            be met.

       ii) Calculations and exhibits showing whether stormwater detention is necessary per
           the requirements of Section 4.8. This includes:

            (1) Existing and proposed tributary area maps that show:

               (a) Offsite and onsite tributary areas:

               (b) Subcatchment tributary areas, showing:

                   (i) Boundaries, with consideration for project phasing, if applicable.

                   (ii) Acreages.

                   (iii) Assumed uses and corresponding runoff curve numbers and/or
                         coefficients.

               (c) Existing and proposed storm and drainage structures.

               (d) Proposed and existing contours.

            (2) Critical storm calculations.

   e) A traffic study, if deemed necessary by the requirements of Section 2.2.



4) Construction Plans
   a) All Developments
Upon completion of the zoning review process, construction plans shall be submitted for the
development, or the phase of which is intended to be constructed. The list below details
submittal items required for all developments and is intended to communicate the level of detail
required within a plan submitted for review. Further requirements for construction plans are
included within parts b) and c) of this subsection, depending on whether the development has
substantial levels of public improvements. The Village may request additional details to help
facilitate their review if those submitted are not adequate to determine compliance with the
Village’s regulations.
       i)   Cover Sheet, including:
            (1) The development name.
            (2) An index map labeling major roads in the Village and indicating the project’s
                location within the Village.

Engineering Design Standards                                                                Page 8
Village of Plain City, Ohio


           (3) An overall plan view showing:
               (a) The proposed improvements.
               (b) Internal and adjacent property lines, rights-of-way, and their respective
                   owners.
               (c) Adjacent road names.
               (d) Major features within 100 feet of the development, including structures,
                   detention basins, streams, and ditches.
           (4) Space for signatures of the Village Administrator, Mayor, Village Planner, and
               Village Engineer.
       ii) Village General Notes, detailed in Appendix A
           (1) Notes that are not applicable to the development shall be replaced with “N/A.”

5) As-Built Plans

Upon completion of construction of improvements under a Public Improvement Plan, the Owner
shall correct their plans to show to the “As-Built” conditions of their development and verify the
performance of their stormwater facilities.
       i)   Public improvements will not be accepted by the Village until these as-built
            construction drawings and verifications are delivered and accepted.
       ii) One (1) full size (22" x 34") copy, and one (1) half size (11" x 17") sets of drawings,
           an electronic file in AutoCAD DWG format, and Excel spreadsheet in .xls format,
           using a template accepted by the Village.
       iii) The “As-Built” drawing shall show changes in the construction as recorded by a
            Professional Surveyor registered in the State of Ohio.
       iv) For projects constructing stormwater retention or detention facilities, a certification by
           the Professional Engineer who prepared the plans shall be provided that verifies that
           the retention/detention facilities were constructed and perform per the project’s
           Construction Plans. Supporting calculations and reporting shall be submitted with
           this certification.

Section 2 – Public Streets
1) Public Street Design

a) All public streets shall be designed and constructed to meet the criteria established within
   this section.
b) Private streets shall be designed to preserve the health, safety, and welfare of the public.
   Designs for private streets are subject to the approval of the Village Engineer during their
   review of the associated Construction Plan.
c) The determination of classifications for roads are guided by the Ohio Department of
   Transportation Highway Functional Classification System or as determined by the Village.
d) Existing streets within the Village are classified as shown in Appendix B.
e) Roadway design standards are dependent on the projected traffic volumes for the road
   being designed. This projection shall include all traffic generated by the development being
   considered as well as the additional traffic generated by its interconnection to future
   developments to ensure the adequacy of design as development progresses.
f)   The Ohio Department of Transportation Location & Design Manual, Volume 1 – Roadway
     Design (ODOT L&D Manual) shall be the basis of design for roads within the Village.
g) For roads with a traffic volume of less than 2,000 ADT (projected or actual), the AASHTO
   Guidelines for Geometric Design of Low-Volume Roads, most recent edition, shall
   supersede the requirements of the ODOT L&D Manual.
h) Right-of-way widths are dependent on the street classification and are as follows:
           i.    Arterial: 100 feet
          ii.    Major Collector: 80 feet
          iii.   Industrial: 80 feet
          iv.    Minor Collector: 70 feet
          v.     Local: 60 feet
i)   If a proposed development fronts an existing roadway that does not meet the requirements
     of this manual or the sections established with the Standard Drawings, the Village shall
     require that it be improved to meet these standards. These standards include, but are not
     limited to, right-of-way widths, street layout, and pavement composition.
j)   The design and improvement of proposed and existing arterial roads shall be made on a
     project-specific basis depending on the project being considered, the distribution of traffic,
     and the uses accessed by the road. Any development along an arterial road will be required,
     at a minimum, to provide the right-of-way width required by this section for an arterial road.
k) Pavement shall meet or exceed criteria outlined within the typical pavement section shown
   within the standard drawings.

Engineering Design Standards                                                               Page 13
Village of Plain City, Ohio


l)   Bridges shall be designed in conformance with the latest edition of the Ohio Department of
     Transportation Bridge Design Manual. Calculations and designs shall be submitted to the
     Village to demonstrate that these standards have been met.
m) Guard posts or barricades are required at the end of streets which are to be extended in the
   future.
n) A T-turnaround shall be provided for dead-end streets exceeding 200 feet in length.
o) The distance between the centerlines of roads intersecting the same roadway shall be a
   minimum of 150 feet apart.
p) Sidewalks and/or shared use paths shall be constructed per the Village’s standard drawings
   along both sides of the road.
q) Sidewalks shall extend to the curbs at all intersections and shall include wheelchair ramps
   meeting ADA requirements and the Village’s standard drawings.
r) Shared use paths may be required along property frontages and be constructed as per the
   appropriate standard drawing.
s) Driveway aprons shall be constructed per the appropriate standard drawing.
t)   All traffic, street name signs, and pavement markings shall be installed by the developer
     a) Signing and striping shall conform to the requirements of the Ohio Manual of Uniform
        Traffic Control Devices and the Village Engineer.
     b) Street name signs shall be designed in accordance with the appropriate Village standard
        drawing, unless otherwise allowed by the Village Engineer.



2) Traffic Impact Study
     1) To promote efficient access management, a Traffic Impact Study (TIS) for a proposed
        development shall be submitted when the development will generate more than 200 trips
        in any peak hour, based on information obtained from the most recent version of the
        Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE) Trip Generation Manual.

     2) The trip generation calculations shall be submitted with the Site Plan application or
        Preliminary Development Plan, whichever is applicable.

     3) Prior to the submission of a Traffic Impact Study, it is recommended that a Memorandum
        of Understanding be agreed to with the Village that establishes the parameters and
        assumptions of the study.

     4) If required, the Traffic Impact Study shall be submitted with the Final Development Plan
        (for PUD developments) or the Construction Plans (for non-PUD developments). Internal
        trip estimates presented in terms of Average Daily Traffic shall also be included at these
        stages to determine roadway classifications per Part 1) e) of this Section.


Engineering Design Standards                                                               Page 14
Village of Plain City, Ohio


   5) The Traffic Impact Study shall in general meet the requirements of the Ohio Department
      of Transportation’s State Highway Access Management Manual (SHAMM), Section 9.4.
      The Village reserves the right to modify these requirements on a case-by-case basis.

   6) Mitigating Traffic Impacts

           a. If the TIS results in the conclusion that the level of service of adjacent streets
              and/or intersections is deficient or will become so after construction of the subject
              development, the developer will be responsible for the mitigation of these
              deficiencies.

           b. Deficient service is defined as a level of service below the operational goals
              established by the ODOT Analysis and Traffic Simulation manual, as shown
              below:
                                 Result                 Operational Goal

                          Intersection LOS                  D or Better

                           Approach LOS                     E or Better

                               Control LOS                  E or Better

Section 3 – Public Street Lighting
1) Street lighting shall be designed and installed by the developer following the City of
   Columbus Street Lighting Design Guide, most recent edition, as modified by this section,
   and is subject to the review, approval, and acceptance of the Village.
2) Light poles and luminaires are subject to the Village’s approval and shall be in accordance
   with their current design standards.
3) Costs for powering light fixtures shall be the responsibility of the developer until the street
   lighting system is accepted by the Village. Billing accounts shall be organized such that
   each lighting control system receives its own bill for its corresponding lighting fixtures.
4) Lighting plans and calculations are required for the installation of all public street lights and
   shall be subject to the following requirements:
   a) Plan Contents
       i)   Lighting plans shall be prepared and sealed by a Professional Engineer registered in
            the State of Ohio.
       ii) A single-line diagram shall be provided that shows:
            (1) The circuit routing through the development.
            (2) All modifications to existing circuit routes.
            (3) Stations and offsets of the following, relative to the centerline of the right-of-way:
                (a) Transformers and controllers.
                (b) Light poles
                (c) Pull boxes
       iii) A photometric plan shall be provided that shows:
            (1) Illumination levels throughout the project.
            (2) A summary schedule detailing:
                (a) The average illumination and uniformity ratio.
                (b) The target value established by the City of Columbus Street Lighting Design
                    Guide for each use (Roadway, Sidewalk, and Intersection).
                (c) Separate lines on the summary schedule shall be provided for each use to
                    ensure compliance with the requirements for each use, including a separate
                    line for the sidewalk or shared-use path on each side of the road.
       iv) Calculations detailing voltage drops shall be calculated per the City of Columbus
           Street Lighting Design Guide.

Section 4 – Drainage
1) Governing Standards

   a) For items not covered within this manual, the Village may utilize the City of Columbus
      Stormwater Drainage Manual and/or the Ohio Department of Natural Resource’s
      Rainwater and Land Development guide to specify drainage and storm water
      management practices within the Village.


2) Grading Plans

Where required, grading plans shall be submitted and show:
   a) Ground elevations with existing and proposed contours shown at intervals of not more
      than 5 feet where the slope is greater than ten percent (10%) and not more than 1 feet
      where the slope is less than ten percent (10%).
   b) Sufficient proposed elevations, such as at all lot corners, local high and low points, etc.,
      to detail the proposed grading and drainage pattern. Additional details may be requested
      if the grading design is not fully apparent.
   c) Finished floor and ground elevations of all existing and proposed structures.
   d) Flood routing across the site, including cross sections at critical points.
   e) Elevations of proposed and existing storm sewer structures.


3) Site Drainage

   a) Swales necessary to carry surface water must have a minimum gradient of one percent.
   b) The minimum building elevation adjacent to the 100-year routing path shall be set a
      minimum of 1 foot above the 100-year flood elevation. No basement entrances,
      windows, or basement level garages shall be permitted adjacent to and below the 100-
      year routing path.
   c) The maximum desired slope in yard or open areas is 4:1.




Engineering Design Standards                                                              Page 17
Village of Plain City, Ohio


4) Easements

   a) Flood routes on private property are required to be under easement.
       i)   Easements shall be at least equal to the area required to carry the 100-year rainfall.
       ii) The easement shall be shown on the plat as a "Watercourse and Utility Easement."
           Restrictions as to the use of this easement shall be shown on the plat.
       iii) No buildings, plantings, or other improvements shall be permitted within that
            easement.
   b) Open watercourses shall be under easement.
       i)   Such easements shall incorporate area required to carry the 100-year rainfall plus an
            additional 15 feet on each side of this area.
       ii) These easements are to be kept free of obstructions.
       iii) Detailed provisions regarding the entities to be responsible for maintenance of the
            facility shall be submitted in text form with the plat. As applicable, notes regarding
            maintenance shall be made on the plat.


5) Storm Sewer Design Criteria

   a) The design of systems draining less than 200 acres of area shall be prepared using the
      Rational Method and shall be based on a minimum 2-year frequency.
       i)   Rainfall intensity shall be per the National Weather Service’s Precipitation Frequency
            Data Server for the project site.
       ii) Runoff coefficients shall be as established by the City of Columbus Stormwater
           Drainage Manual.
       iii) Time of concentration shall be equal to the duration of time required for runoff to flow
            from the most remote part of the drainage area to the point under design. The
            minimum time of concentration shall be 10 minutes.
   b) For drainage areas over 200 acres, the method explained in "Urban Hydrology for Small
      Watershed, Technical Release No. 55" (known as TR-55) shall be used.
   c) All areas which contribute storm water to the proposed drainage system must be
      considered to determine of the sizes of structures and channels, including those entering
      the system from offsite.
   d) Storm sewer pipe sizes are to be determined by using Manning's Formula with a
      minimum coefficient of roughness of n = .013.
   e) Storm sewers shall be designed to provide a minimum allowable velocity of 3 feet per
      second (fps) when the pipe flows full. The maximum allowable velocity shall be 7 fps.



Engineering Design Standards                                                                 Page 18
Village of Plain City, Ohio


   f)   A hydraulic grade line check based on a 5-year storm may be required at the discretion
        of the Village Engineer. The hydraulic grade line for the 5-year storm event shall stay
        beneath the rim elevation of all structures along the storm sewer.
   g) The minimum cover for storm sewers shall be 30 inches.
   h) Pipe for storm sewers shall not be less than 12 inches in diameter and be designed for a
      minimum of an HS-20 live load condition.
   i)   The flow lines of pipes shall be set such that either the crown or the 0.8 depth points at
        junctions are at the same elevation. However, the crown of the outlet pipe may be lower.
   j)   Storm sewers connected to bodies of water shall be designed to ensure that upstream
        structures do not carry standing water at normal water elevations.


6) Storm Sewer Layout and Construction

   a) Storm sewer structures and construction practices are to be per the Village’s standard
      drawings.
   b) Headwalls or endwalls are to be constructed at the inlet and/or outfall of all storm sewers
      and shall be shown on the plan and profile.
   c) The inverts of all curb inlets, manholes, yard inlets, and other appurtenances shall be
      formed to reduce turbulence to a minimum.
   d) Manholes shall be provided at all changes in alignment and grade of storm sewers and
      at such other locations as necessary to maintain a maximum interval of 300 feet
      between manholes.
   e) The maximum distance for overland flow shall be 300 feet before entering a surface yard
      inlet or 400 feet before entering a curb inlet, except that the maximum overland drainage
      area tributary to any yard inlet or curb inlet shall not exceed 1.5 acres. Structures
      collecting off-site runoff are exempt from these requirements, but remain subject to the
      flood routing and storm sewer performance requirements of this section.
   f)   The maximum spacing for curb inlets shall not exceed 400 feet unless approved by the
        Village Engineer.
   g) The maximum spread of flow during a 2-year storm shall not exceed 8 feet for 30-foot
      wide streets and 9 feet for streets wider than 30 feet. Spread calculations may be
      required at the discretion of the Village Engineer.


7) Open Watercourses

    a) Where a 72-inch pipe is inadequate for a 2-year storm, an open watercourse may be
       permitted.



Engineering Design Standards                                                              Page 19
Village of Plain City, Ohio


    b) Design requirements:
        i)      The design storm shall be a 10-year storm, with a 1-foot freeboard.
        ii) The minimum velocity for open channels shall be 2 feet per second.
        iii) The maximum velocity is dependent on the type of channel protection provided.
        iv) The minimum desirable grade for open channel is 0.4 percent (.4%).
        v) The Manning "n" values for the channel lining shall be as detailed within the City of
           Columbus Stormwater Drainage Manual, latest edition, or as required by the Village
           Engineer.
        vi) Side slopes shall be 3:1 or milder, with a minimum 2-foot bottom width. Slopes
            adjacent to roadways shall be 4:1 or milder.
   b) If the proposed improvements are located in a floodplain area as identified by the
      Federal Emergency Management Agency, the limits of this floodway and floodway fringe
      must be shown on the improvement plans.



8) Roadway Culverts

   a) Single-span culverts, including concrete box or slab top, should always be considered in
      lieu of multiple-cell pipe culverts in order to meet the physical requirements introduced
      by rigid headwater controls.
   b) The plan for each culvert shall indicate the drainage area in acres and the design
      discharge in cubic feet per second.
   c) The culvert invert elevation should be set such that it will be deep enough to provide an
      adequate outlet for future storm sewer improvements upstream.
   d) The design storm shall be as per Section 1103 of the ODOT Location and Design
      Manual, Volume 2 – Drainage Design:
              i.    For traveled ways with 3000 ADT or more: 25-year.
             ii.    For traveled ways under 3000 ADT: 10-year.
             iii.   For pedestrian or bicycle routes: 5-year.
   e) Culverts shall be designed in accordance with the Ohio Department of Transportation
      Location & Design Manual, Volume 2 – Drainage Design.
   f)    Design calculations for all culverts shall be approved by the Village Engineer.




Engineering Design Standards                                                               Page 20
Village of Plain City, Ohio


9) Stormwater Detention

   a) Stormwater detention must be provided in accordance with the following table:

                  Percent Increase in 1-year Volume Runoff        Control Design Frequency
            Equal to or Greater Than          And Less Than            (Critical Storm)

                    --                             10                     1 year
                    10                             20                     2 year
                    20                             50                     5 year
                    50                             100                    10 year
                    100                            250                    25 year
                    250                            500                    50 year
                    500                            --                     100 year

        Changes in stormwater runoff shall be determined using the runoff curve number
        method described in NRCS Technical Release 55.
    b) Runoff from storm events less than or equal to the critical storm event shall be released
       from the site at a rate no greater than the peak runoff during a 1-year storm event under
       pre-developed conditions. The maximum allowable release rate for storms greater than
       the critical storm shall not exceed the predeveloped rate for the same frequency storm,
       for storms up to and including the 100-year storm.
    c) Design of stormwater detention facilities shall be in accordance with the Ohio Rainwater
       and Land Development Manual.
    d) All control facilities shall be designed with overflow provisions to handle the developed
       100-year discharge.


10) Required Submissions
   a) Where development activities require drainage improvements, including storm sewers,
      open watercourses, and/or stormwater detention, developers shall also submit drainage
      calculations, exhibits, and reporting within a Storm Water Management Report that
      shows that the requirements of this section are met. This may include:

       i)     Existing and proposed tributary area maps, including:

              (1) Offsite and onsite tributary areas:

              (2) Subcatchment tributary areas, showing:

                  (a) Boundaries

                  (b) Acreages

                  (c) Assumed uses and corresponding runoff curve numbers and/or coefficients.



Engineering Design Standards                                                                 Page 21
Village of Plain City, Ohio


           (3) Existing and proposed storm and drainage structures.

           (4) Proposed and existing contours.

       ii) Soil maps.

       iii) HydroCAD outputs (or approved equivalent) comparing pre- and post-development
            runoff conditions.

       iv) Ditch or spillway capacity calculations.

       v) Flood route calculations.

       vi) Spread calculations.

       vii) Storm sewer design calculations.

       viii) A written narrative report summarizing the drainage design and calculations.

       ix) Additional materials may be requested by the Village to adequately review the
           drainage design.
